templates.title: Systems, products and services inventory
templates.description: Implements ID.IM-P1: Systems, products, and services that process data are inventoried.

title.en: Define the boundary of the processing inventory

description.en: State which systems, products and services are in scope of the inventory, the criterion that puts one in or out, and who settles a disputed case. Attach the scoping statement naming the business units, sites and hosting arrangements it covers, so a later completeness check has a denominator to measure against.

title.en: Record each system, product and service that processes data

description.en: For every entity inside the boundary, capture its name, the owner or operator accountable for it, the roles involved in running the processing, and the environment it runs in — where it is located and whether it is internal, hosted, or operated by another party. Attach the inventory as it stands when the entries are complete.

title.en: Reconcile the inventory against an independent source

description.en: Compare the inventory against at least one source not derived from it — procurement records, expenditure records, or owners' own declarations — and record every entity that appears in one and not the other. Record how each discrepancy was resolved and which side was wrong.

evidenceHint.en: Dated reconciliation worksheet naming the independent source used, each discrepancy found, and its resolution.

title.en: Test the inventory against the systems retired or acquired since the last pass

description.en: An inventory decays at its edges, not in the middle: the long-standing systems stay right while a decommissioned service lingers as an entry and a newly bought or inherited one never appears. Take the period's joiners and leavers from the sources that know — procurement, cloud billing, the change log, any acquisition — and check each against the inventory, rather than re-reading the inventory to see whether it looks complete. A retired system still listed is as much a defect as a missing one, because every later assessment treats it as live.

evidenceHint.en: Period comparison naming each system acquired, inherited or retired, the source it was drawn from, and the inventory entry added, closed or found already correct.

templates.title: Owners, operators and processing roles
templates.description: Implements ID.IM-P2: Owners or operators and roles for data processing are inventoried.

title.en: Set the test that separates an accountable owner from a day-to-day operator

description.en: Without a stated test the register fills with whoever answered first, and the same activity acquires an owner on one line and an operator on another. Write the test down: accountability sits with whoever can stop, change or approve the processing and must answer for it, while operating means running it under that authority; administrators, reviewers and approvers are recorded but carry no accountability. State how many holders an activity may have, and name who decides when two people claim one activity or nobody does. This is about who inside the organisation answers for the processing, not the organisation's own standing toward other parties.

evidenceHint.en: Role definition note stating which holder types may appear, how answering for processing is distinguished from running it, the limit on holders per activity, and who arbitrates a contested entry.

title.en: Name the person accountable for each processing activity and the party that operates it

description.en: A team label is not an accountability holder: when the entry reads "Platform" there is nobody to answer for a decision about the data. Capture a named holder for each activity, and separately the party that actually runs it day to day, which is often a different team or an outside supplier. Where no one will accept an entry, leave it marked unheld rather than blank, so the gap is countable instead of invisible.

evidenceHint.en: Register of processing activities with, for each, a named accountability holder, the team or supplier running it, the date the name was accepted, and the entries still unheld.

title.en: Ask each named owner to state what they are accountable for

description.en: An owner entered without the holder's knowledge looks like a filled field and behaves like an empty one. Put the question to the holder rather than to their manager, and compare the answer with the register: where someone describes a narrower remit than the register gives them, the remainder is unheld and needs reassigning. Refusals and disputes go to whoever can actually move the accountability, not back into the register unchanged.

evidenceHint.en: Confirmation record showing who was asked, what each said they hold, the mismatches against the register, and where every disputed or refused entry was escalated.

templates.title: Categories of individuals whose data is processed
templates.description: Implements ID.IM-P3: Categories of individuals whose data are processed are inventoried.

title.en: Settle which categories of individuals the organisation will distinguish, and why

description.en: Agree the label set before anyone starts tagging entries, with a definition and an example for each, or one team writes customers, another users and a third data subjects for the same people and the inventory can never be totalled or searched by population. The set must carry explicit labels for the groups that change what is owed — minors, patients, employees, job applicants, and people who have never dealt with the organisation — since a generic label hides exactly the populations a later assessment needs to find. Also state the rule for someone who meets two definitions at once, such as an employee who is also a customer, so an entry records both rather than whichever the tagger thought of first.

evidenceHint.en: Approved label set with a definition and worked example for each, the treatment of a person meeting two definitions, and dated sign-off from the owner who settled it.

title.en: Name every category of individual whose data each system holds

description.en: Against each inventory entry, list the kinds of people whose data actually ends up in it rather than the kinds the system was built to serve — the two diverge wherever a record describes someone who never dealt with the organisation, such as an emergency contact, a referred friend, a dependant on a policy, a person named in a free-text support note, or an address book uploaded by a user. Categories that attract extra obligations — children, patients, employees, job applicants — have to be named in their own right, because the duty follows the category and disappears the moment it is folded into a general bucket labelled users or contacts. Where a category appears only occasionally, list it anyway and note the route by which those people arrive.

evidenceHint.en: Per-entry register naming each population present, the route by which it enters, whether those people transacted with the organisation at all, and the owner who confirmed the entry.

title.en: Sample live records to find people no declared category accounts for

description.en: A category list assembled from design documents describes the intended population, not the one in the tables, so check it against real rows: pull a sample from each store and work out who each row is about, including people mentioned inside another person's record. Absence needs evidence as much as presence — a system listed as holding no children's data usually earns that listing by never asking for age, which is not the same as the population being absent, so look for the attributes that would betray them (date of birth, school, guardian, relationship-to-account-holder) before accepting the claim. Anyone found who fits none of the declared categories is the finding, and each one gets a correction to the entry and a named owner.

evidenceHint.en: Sampling note per store recording what was examined, each person encountered who matched no listed population, the sensitive populations tested for and the basis for every claimed absence, and the corrections raised.

templates.title: Data actions inventory
templates.description: Implements ID.IM-P4: Data actions of the systems, products, and services are inventoried.

title.en: Settle which operations count as a data action and when one splits in two

description.en: Collection, use, sharing, storage and disposal read as five clean categories until two teams describe the same nightly export as one operation and as four. Fix the list of operation types an entry may draw on, and the rule that decides when a single step is written as one line or several — for instance whether a read followed by a transformation into a second store counts once or twice. Without that rule entries cannot be compared across teams, and counting how many data actions are inventoried tells nobody anything.

evidenceHint.en: Agreed definition sheet naming each permitted operation type, with worked examples of a step kept whole and a step written as several.

title.en: Describe the data actions, purposes, elements and individuals for each entry

description.en: Against each inventory entry, record what is done with the data, why each of those actions is performed, which data elements each touches, and which categories of individuals the data relates to. Where one entry serves several purposes, record them separately rather than collapsing them into one line.

title.en: Check whether any system performs a data action absent from its entry

description.en: A list of operations decays quietly: a new export job appears, a copy is written to a second store, or the script that was deleting old records stops running, and none of that changes what is written down. Sit with the people who run each system and walk its scheduled jobs, integrations and deletion routines, marking every operation with no matching line in the entry. Record both directions of the gap — operations performed but never listed, and listed operations the system no longer carries out.

evidenceHint.en: Walkthrough notes for each system listing every operation found with no matching line, and the lines closed off as no longer carried out.

templates.title: Purposes for each data action
templates.description: Implements ID.IM-P5: The purposes for the data actions are inventoried.

title.en: Set how specific a purpose must be before it counts as stated

description.en: Left to each author, entries settle on wording like "business operations" or "improving the service" that fits every action and therefore excludes none, and the inventory loses the ability to say whether a proposed new use is already covered. Decide the level of detail required — a reason an individual would recognise as distinct from the next one — name the wording entries must draw from so one reason is not written three ways, and say who rules on a disputed entry. Settle this before entries are written: re-wording several hundred of them later is how the rule quietly stops being applied.

evidenceHint.en: The agreed wording rule with worked examples of an acceptable and an unacceptable entry, and the named arbiter.

title.en: Pin each purpose to the data action it justifies, not to the system

description.en: A reason written against a whole system — "CRM: managing customers" — cannot answer whether a particular collection or onward disclosure was warranted, because one system carries several actions performed for different reasons. Against every action already listed, write the reason it is carried out, and where one action serves several reasons list them separately rather than joining them with "and". Mark which reason prompted the data to be obtained in the first place and which were added afterwards, with the date each later one began, so a use bolted on after the fact is visible as such.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory export listing, against every action, the reasons held for it and when each was added.

title.en: Retire each recorded purpose the organisation has stopped pursuing

description.en: Reasons accumulate and are almost never withdrawn: a feature is switched off, the collection that fed it keeps running, and a purpose nobody pursues goes on justifying it. Walk the list with the people who own each activity and mark it still pursued or not; for every one that is not, record whether the action stopped too, or now runs for some other reason that must itself be written down. Where an action continues and nobody can name a live reason for it, raise that as a finding instead of fitting a plausible reason to it.

evidenceHint.en: Marked-up list from the sweep showing which activities were confirmed live, and the disposition of the rest.

templates.title: Data elements within each data action
templates.description: Implements ID.IM-P6: Data elements within the data actions are inventoried.

title.en: Set the granularity at which a field counts as one data element

description.en: Without a stated counting rule one team writes down contact details and another writes down eleven columns, and the two lists can be neither compared nor totalled. Decide whether a structured blob, a free-text note and an attached document are each one element or many, how a repeating group is counted, and whether a derived score sits beside the inputs it was calculated from. State which source of truth a name is taken from, so the same attribute is not entered twice under a column name and a form label.

evidenceHint.en: The written counting rule with worked examples covering a nested object, a repeating group, an uploaded document and a calculated value.

title.en: Enumerate the fields and attributes each data action touches

description.en: Work from the schemas, request payloads and form definitions rather than from a system's documentation, and name the individual fields each action reads and each one it writes. Derived and inferred attributes are elements too, and they are the ones most often missed because no interface ever asked for them. Free-text notes and uploaded files count as well, since whatever a person typed into them is held all the same. Where an action touches an entire table, list its columns instead of the table name.

evidenceHint.en: The per-action field list with each entry traced to the schema column, API contract or capture form it came from, and derived values marked as such.

title.en: Pull a live record and check each field on it was inventoried

description.en: An element list assembled from documentation drifts the moment a release adds a column or a vendor response grows a new key. Take a real record out of each significant store, list every populated attribute on it, and mark those no inventory entry accounts for. The opposite drift matters as much: elements still listed for fields the system stopped populating make the inventory read as more complete than it is.

evidenceHint.en: The extracted record's attribute list matched line by line against entries, with unmatched names in both directions called out and dated.

templates.title: The data processing environment
templates.description: Implements ID.IM-P7: The data processing environment is identified (e.g., geographic location, internal, cloud, third parties).

title.en: Settle the environment facts every entry must carry, and what counts as a jurisdiction

description.en: Without an agreed vocabulary one team writes "EU", another writes a region code and a third writes the vendor's name, and none of the three answers whether data left a jurisdiction. Fix up front the location granularity required, the internal-versus-external distinction, the cloud, on-premise and hybrid distinction, and which legal regimes this organisation treats as separate. Name who rules on an entry that spans several of them, such as a replicated database or a support desk that follows the sun.

evidenceHint.en: The agreed attribute definitions and permitted values, with a worked example for a multi-region system and the named arbiter

title.en: Pin every system to its hosting country, facility and provider

description.en: An entry reading "the cloud" or just the provider's brand name cannot answer a transfer question. For each inventoried system capture the provider's own region and zone identifiers, the physical site for anything on-premise, whether the organisation or an outside party runs that hosting, and the legal regime the site sits under. A system that fails over or replicates into a second region has two environments, and both belong on the entry.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory export showing region, site, internal-or-external and jurisdiction values for each entry, with the provider documentation the region names were taken from

title.en: Derive each system's hosting location from the provider console, not the inventory

description.en: Regions get enabled, workloads get migrated and backups get replicated into new countries without anyone opening the inventory, so an entry that was correct when written drifts in silence. Pull the live region, zone and account list from each provider's console or API and set it against what the entry claims, one entry at a time. Where the two disagree, note which side changed and when, so the next pass can tell a stale record from an unannounced migration.

evidenceHint.en: Console or API output listing live regions and accounts alongside the matching entries, with every difference and the date it was traced to

templates.title: The data processing map
templates.description: Implements ID.IM-P8: Data processing is mapped, illustrating the data actions and associated data elements for systems, products, and services.

title.en: Settle the notation and granularity of the data-flow map

description.en: Before anyone draws, fix what a box on the map stands for — one system, one service, or one data action — and how a data element is attached to a line between them. Two people mapping at different levels produce pictures that cannot be joined: one draws a single CRM box where the other draws six actions, and neither version can be reconciled against the inventory entries. Decide the notation to be used and the minimum every line must carry — source, destination, what happens to the data there, and which elements travel — so each drawer produces the same kind of picture.

evidenceHint.en: Convention note stating the chosen notation, what a box and a line each represent, and the minimum detail every flow must carry.

title.en: Draw the map linking data actions to data elements across entries

description.en: Produce a representation — in whatever form the organisation already uses to describe its systems — showing how data moves between inventoried entries, which action occurs at each point, and which data elements are involved. Attach the map and name which inventory entries it covers and which it does not.

title.en: Review the inventory and map against the scope statement

description.en: Confirm that every entity inside the stated boundary carries an owner, purposes, data elements, categories of individuals and an environment, and appears on the map. Record each gap found together with the person who will close it.

evidenceHint.en: Review record naming the reviewer, the entries checked, and the gaps raised with an owner against each.

templates.title: The organisation's role in the ecosystem
templates.description: Implements ID.BE-P1: The organization's role(s) in the data processing ecosystem are identified and communicated.

title.en: State the organisation's role in each data processing relationship

description.en: For every relationship in which data passes to or from another party, record what the organisation does with the data, what the other party does, and which side decides why the processing happens at all. Attach the resulting statement of roles, one entry per relationship.

title.en: Split any relationship in which the organisation acts as both processor and controller

description.en: One counterparty usually sits on both sides at once: a vendor handles customer records strictly on instruction, and under the same agreement collects usage telemetry it decides to analyse for its own product work — processor for the first, controller in its own right for the second. Carrying one role per counterparty hides the second half, and the hidden half is what produces a subject request the organisation wrongly sends elsewhere, or terms drafted for the side it is not on. Give each flow its own entry, with the answer to who chose the purpose and who chose the means, and reserve joint controller for flows where both genuinely chose together instead of pushing the call onto one party.

evidenceHint.en: Register extract showing each counterparty split into its own entries, with the purpose-and-means answer recorded beside each.

title.en: Communicate the role statement to the parties it names

description.en: Make the statement available to each party it describes, through whatever channel that relationship already uses, and record which party received which version and when. Where a party disputes the role attributed to it, record the dispute and how it was settled.

evidenceHint.en: Distribution record showing each party, the version issued, the date, and any dispute raised and its outcome.

title.en: Re-test each controller or processor designation against the year's actual use

description.en: Compare the designation on file with what was actually done with the data over the period: a purpose added to a flow the organisation previously only hosted, telemetry turned to the organisation's own analysis, a sub-provider engaged on the organisation's own initiative rather than on a client's instruction. Each of those flips the answer to who chose the purpose and the means, while the designation set at onboarding sits untouched because no contract was reopened and nothing in the relationship looked like it moved. List every designation re-tested, which ones changed and why, and which flows are now held pending a decision on the role.

evidenceHint.en: Dated note naming the flows re-examined, the label each now carries, and what moved it.

templates.title: Organisational priorities for data processing
templates.description: Implements ID.BE-P2: Priorities for organizational mission, objectives, and activities are established and communicated.

title.en: Name the body that ranks mission objectives and the audiences it must reach

description.en: Without one body owning the ranking, two committees publish competing orders and a team facing a privacy trade-off cites whichever order suits it. Name the forum that settles the order, the person who breaks a tie when two objectives conflict, and the standing recipients — processing owners, engineering leads, and the parties acting on the organisation's behalf — who must be sent the ranking rather than left to find it. Fix the channel for each recipient at this point, so the later communication step works from a distribution list it did not have to invent.

evidenceHint.en: Scoping note naming the deciding forum, the tie-breaker for conflicting objectives, and each standing recipient with the channel used.

title.en: Record the organisational priorities that depend on data processing

description.en: List the mission and business objectives the organisation is pursuing that rely on processing data, in priority order, with the reason each sits where it does. This is the list a later privacy trade-off is argued against, so it must be specific enough for an argument to be lost against it.

title.en: Review the role statement and priority list against current activity

description.en: Compare both documents against the relationships and services the organisation actually runs today, record every change since the last review, and update them. Name anything found running that appears on neither list, and who will decide where it belongs.

evidenceHint.en: Dated review note listing the relationships and priorities checked and each change made or ruled unnecessary.

templates.title: Systems supporting organisational priorities
templates.description: Implements ID.BE-P3: Systems/products/services that support organizational priorities are identified and key requirements communicated.

title.en: Set the dependency test each priority's supporting systems must pass

description.en: State what a system must do for a priority to fail without it, and how far down the stack that judgement is carried — the database beneath an application and the identity provider it authenticates against either count or they do not, and the answer has to be the same for every priority. Without that rule one priority names three systems and the next names the whole estate, and the two lists can be neither compared nor resourced. Name who settles a contested case and where the agreed test is written down.

evidenceHint.en: Scoping note stating the criterion, the depth it is applied to, the decision-maker for contested cases, and the date it was agreed.

title.en: Link each priority to the systems it depends on and state their key requirements

description.en: For every priority, name the systems, products or services it could not survive without, and record what each must deliver for the priority to hold — availability, accuracy, confidentiality, or something else. Record who those requirements have been communicated to and when.

title.en: Confirm the supporting systems and their key requirements still match today's priorities

description.en: Set the priority list beside the dependency record and mark every pairing that has stopped being true: a priority now carried by a different service, a system retired or folded into another, a stated requirement that no longer describes what the priority needs from it. The break that survives longest is a change of operator — after a migration or a supplier switch the requirement is still held against people who no longer run the system, so check each requirement against whoever operates it today. Note every correction made and who made it, and name any priority left resting on nothing.

evidenceHint.en: Dated review note pairing every priority with the services now carrying it, each pairing corrected, and the current operator holding each stated requirement.

templates.title: Contextual factors around data actions
templates.description: Implements ID.RA-P1: Contextual factors related to the systems/products/services and the data actions are identified (e.g., individuals' demographics, visibility into processing, data sensitivity).

title.en: Record the contextual factors surrounding each data action assessed

description.en: For each data action taken from the processing map, capture the factors that shape how a person would experience it: who the individuals are, how visible the processing is to them, how sensitive the data is, and the setting the action occurs in. These factors are the input the assessment is reasoned from, so record them before any judgement of risk is made.

title.en: Grade sensitivity, visibility and individuals' ability to decline on defined scales

description.en: A data element is not equally sensitive everywhere: a home address is unremarkable for a delivery and dangerous when the person is hiding from someone, so the grade belongs to the data action in its circumstances, not to the field. Write down what each level means — including what makes processing imperceptible to the person and what makes declining it impractical — so a second assessor lands on the same level without asking the author. Where each assessor invents a private meaning for 'sensitive', two assessments of the same system cannot be compared or escalated on the same footing.

evidenceHint.en: The definition sheet for each factor scale, together with the graded entries: the level assigned to every data action, the wording it was matched against, and the person who assigned it.

title.en: Re-test the recorded context where the population changed but the system did not

description.en: Context goes stale with no code changing: a product taken up by a much younger population, a reseller placing it in schools, a press cycle that makes the processing common knowledge, sign-ups arriving from a country nobody considered. A re-assessment trigger keyed to system change fires for none of these, so this pass runs on its own schedule and reads sources outside the assessment — who holds accounts now, what the support and complaint intake shows, how the product is being sold today. List every factor still resting on the assumption first written down, naming the person who will re-establish it or retire it.

evidenceHint.en: Dated pass naming each factor entry, the outside source consulted against it, whether the entry still holds, and every assumption carried forward with an owner.

templates.title: Bias in analytic inputs and outputs
templates.description: Implements ID.RA-P2: Data analytic inputs and outputs are identified and evaluated for bias.

title.en: Settle which analytic outputs are tested for skew and across which groups

description.en: Name the scores, rankings, matches, thresholds and eligibility rules that produce a result about a person, and say for each whether it is in scope. A boundary drawn around machine learning leaves the hand-written rule table and the vendor-supplied score unexamined, which is where the longest-standing disparities usually sit. Record against each in-scope output the data feeding it, since skew is inherited from training sets, reference tables and derived features far more often than it is written into the logic. Name the attributes the comparison will run across and who settles an argument about an exclusion.

evidenceHint.en: Scope list naming each output in scope, the data sets feeding it, the attributes comparison will use, and each exclusion with the reason and who agreed it.

title.en: Evaluate analytic inputs and outputs for bias

description.en: Where processing derives inferences, scores or decisions, record what goes in, what comes out, and the checks made for skew against the categories of individuals recorded in the inventory. Record the result of each check, including the checks that found nothing and the ones that could not be run, with the reason.

title.en: Check how many individuals sat behind each bias result reported clean

description.en: A disparity test returns the same clean verdict whether the outputs really are even across groups or the group that would have failed it is too thin in the sample to shift the figure at all. Take every result recorded as showing no skew, put the number of individuals in each compared group beside it, and mark the ones below the count the method needs before it can detect anything. Re-measure those on a sample drawn to cover the thin groups, and where that cannot be done, move the entry from no skew found to not tested. A result whose model or rule set has since been rebuilt is stale however healthy its group counts were.

evidenceHint.en: Per-result table giving the population count of every compared group, the minimum the method needs to detect a gap, and the re-measurements ordered where that floor was not met.

templates.title: Problematic data actions and their problems
templates.description: Implements ID.RA-P3: Potential problematic data actions and associated problems for individuals are identified.

title.en: Agree the catalogue of harms an individual can suffer from processing

description.en: Write down the kinds of harm the assessment will look for — surveillance, exclusion from a service, unwanted revelation to family or employer, discrimination, financial loss, loss of control over one's own account of oneself — each with a one-line test for recognising it. Without a fixed set, every assessor names only the harms that happen to occur to them, and two systems examined months apart cannot be compared. Keep the catalogue open: an assessor meeting a harm it does not hold adds an entry rather than forcing the nearest fit.

evidenceHint.en: Approved harm catalogue with a recognition test against each entry and the date any entry was added or amended.

title.en: Identify the problems each data action could create for individuals

description.en: For every data action in scope, describe what could go wrong for a person rather than for the organisation — the loss, exposure, exclusion or indignity they would experience — and name the data action that would cause it. Record actions judged to create no problem, with the reason, so the judgement is visible rather than absent.

title.en: Mine complaints and incidents for problematic actions nobody flagged

description.en: Individuals describe what processing did to them through channels never built for privacy work: support tickets, cancellation and refund reasons, sudden account deletions, and letters from a regulator. Read a period's worth, trace each grievance back to the operation on data that produced it, and add any problem the earlier identification never named. A problem people are already reporting that the assessment does not hold is the plainest proof the identification was incomplete.

evidenceHint.en: Dated sweep note naming the channels read, the period covered, and each newly named problem traced to its originating action.

templates.title: Determining and prioritising privacy risk
templates.description: Implements ID.RA-P4: Problematic data actions, likelihoods, and impacts are used to determine and prioritize privacy risk.

title.en: Agree the scoring scales and where the priority line falls

description.en: State what each likelihood and impact band means before any problem is scored — a frequency or plausibility test for likelihood, and an effect on the person rather than a cost to the organisation for impact — and state the score at or above which a problem is treated as a priority. Without those anchors two assessors rate the same data action differently and the two lists cannot be merged into one order. Naming the cut-off first also stops it being shifted afterwards to fit whatever capacity happens to be left, and whoever approves the scales should be told that changing them re-orders every assessment already made.

evidenceHint.en: Approved scoring definitions naming each band, its anchor, the point at which a problem counts as a priority, and the approver.

title.en: Rank the identified problems by likelihood and impact

description.en: Apply the organisation's own likelihood and impact scales to each problem identified and produce a single ordered list. Record the reasoning wherever the ranking runs against expectation, so a reader can see why a severe-sounding problem sits low or a mild one sits high.

title.en: Calibrate the likelihood bands against events that actually occurred

description.en: Take the incidents, complaints and near-misses logged since the last assessment and compare each with the likelihood band the matching problem had been given. A problem rated remote that has now happened twice is evidence about the scale itself, not just about that one entry, so correct the band definitions rather than quietly re-scoring the single line. Check the impact side the same way: an impact judged mild because the organisation absorbed the cost may have been severe for the person it landed on.

evidenceHint.en: Calibration note pairing each observed event with the band it was assigned beforehand, and the definition changes that followed.

templates.title: Identifying and implementing risk responses
templates.description: Implements ID.RA-P5: Risk responses are identified, prioritized, and implemented.

title.en: Turn each chosen response into scheduled work with a named delivery date

description.en: For every response on the register, name the concrete change that delivers it — the configuration change, the process step, the contract amendment, the code change — and the date it is due, so a later check has something specific to look at. Where two responses compete for the same team, sequence them by the rank of the problem they answer rather than by whichever finishes soonest. A response left as an intention with nothing attached to it is the usual reason a problem survives the mitigation that was supposed to remove it.

evidenceHint.en: Plan of agreed mitigations naming, for each, the specific change that carries it out, the team holding it, and the due date set.

title.en: Record the response chosen for each prioritised problem and its owner

description.en: For each problem on the ranked list, state whether it is being reduced, transferred, avoided or accepted, name the person accountable for the response, and record the date the choice was made. Where a problem is accepted, record what is being accepted on the individual's behalf.

evidenceHint.en: Risk response register showing each prioritised problem, the response chosen, its owner and the decision date.

title.en: Verify each recorded response was carried out or re-decided

description.en: Take the responses recorded since the last pass and check whether each reached the state it claims, following the pointer to whatever the owner offers as proof. List every response marked done that has nothing behind it, and every one still open past its own stated intent, with what happens next.

evidenceHint.en: Review record listing each response, its current state, what was offered as proof, and the responses found unsupported.

templates.title: Ecosystem risk management procedures
templates.description: Implements ID.DE-P1: Data processing ecosystem risk management policies, processes, and procedures are identified, established, assessed, managed, and agreed to by stakeholders.

title.en: Settle which relationships the ecosystem privacy policy binds and who may authorise a departure

description.en: Name the relationship types the policy covers — processors, sub-processors, resellers, joint ventures, intra-group transfers, research collaborators — and the ones deliberately left out, with the reason for each exclusion. Without that line drawn, the first arrangement nobody thought of as a supplier is the one that reaches data with no rule attached. State who holds the authority to let an engagement proceed outside the policy, because an exception granted by nobody in particular is indistinguishable from the policy being ignored.

evidenceHint.en: Signed scoping note listing the relationship types inside and outside the policy's reach, the reason for each exclusion, and the named exception authority.

title.en: Agree the ecosystem privacy assessment procedure with the functions that must apply it

description.en: Write down how a party is assessed before an engagement begins and while it runs, who performs the assessment, who may accept a finding, and what stops an engagement. Circulate it to the functions bound by it and record each one's agreement or objection.

title.en: Find the engagements that began without the ecosystem privacy rules being applied

description.en: List the supplier, partner and customer engagements opened since the last review and mark, for each, whether the agreed assessment and approval steps were actually run. For every miss, separate the rule that was skipped from the rule that could not be worked as written — the second is a defect in the procedure, not in the person who bypassed it. Amend the unworkable ones and put each amendment back to the functions that agreed the original, so the version in force stays the version people consented to.

evidenceHint.en: Dated review sheet naming every new arrangement of the period, whether it followed the agreed steps, and the amendments raised as a result.

templates.title: Identifying and prioritising ecosystem parties
templates.description: Implements ID.DE-P2: Data processing ecosystem parties (e.g., service providers, customers, partners, product/service developers) are identified, prioritized, and assessed using a privacy risk assessment process.

title.en: Rank the ecosystem parties by the privacy exposure of what they handle

description.en: Draw the parties from the processing inventory — service providers, customers, partners, developers and anyone else data reaches — record what data each handles and for what, then place them in priority order against stated criteria. Attach the criteria alongside the ranking so a challenge to a party's position can be answered.

title.en: Extend the party list to whoever each provider passes data on to

description.en: A list built from signed agreements stops at the parties the organisation contracted with, while the data keeps travelling — a hosting provider's own hosting provider, a support tool's offshore desk, an analytics vendor's enrichment source. Ask every ranked party to name who else receives or can reach the data, then place those recipients into the same ranking and assessment queue, attributed to the party that introduced them. Where a party will not name them, record the refusal against that party instead of leaving its entry looking complete.

evidenceHint.en: Register entry per newly named recipient recording who disclosed it, what reaches it, and the date it was added; refusals to disclose logged against the party asked.

title.en: Assess each prioritised party against the agreed procedure

description.en: Run the assessment on the parties in priority order, record what was examined and what was found, and note any condition placed on the engagement as a result. Where a party could not be assessed, record why and who accepted proceeding without it.

title.en: Check that each party onboarded since the last review was assessed first

description.en: Take the parties that entered the ecosystem since the last review and compare two dates for each: when its privacy assessment was completed, and when data first reached it. An engagement opened under deadline pressure inverts them, and the assessment then documents an arrangement nobody can still refuse. Record every inversion with the person who authorised the early flow, and state how many new parties were examined so a clean result can be told apart from an empty one.

evidenceHint.en: Dated comparison sheet listing each new party, its assessment completion date, the date data first flowed, and the count of parties examined.

templates.title: Contracts implementing privacy measures
templates.description: Implements ID.DE-P3: Contracts with ecosystem parties are used to implement appropriate measures designed to meet the objectives of the organization's privacy program.

title.en: Set out the privacy terms each class of engagement must carry

description.en: Work out, from the privacy objectives the organisation has set, which measures have to be binding rather than merely requested — return or deletion at exit, limits on onward disclosure and sub-processors, breach notification timing, where processing may happen, a right to evidence — and state which class of engagement each one applies to. Say who may approve a departure and how it is recorded, because pressure to drop a clause arrives at signature rather than at drafting. Cover the case where the organisation signs the counterparty's standard terms and cannot edit them: name which measures an addendum has to carry instead, and which absences make the engagement unacceptable.

evidenceHint.en: Approved schedule of required clauses banded by engagement type, naming the approver and the route for an agreed departure.

title.en: Record the privacy obligations each party is bound to

description.en: Per party, capture the obligations that have actually been agreed with them and where those obligations are written down, including any shared or multi-party arrangement the organisation has joined that carries obligations of its own. Where an assessment identified a needed obligation that was not agreed, record that gap against the party.

title.en: Match the signed terms against the processing each party performs today

description.en: Take each party in the ecosystem ranking, pull the agreement actually in force — base contract plus every amendment, order form and renewal that varies it — and compare the privacy measures it binds the party to with what that party now does with data. Long-standing suppliers commonly run on paper signed before the current clause set existed, and an auto-renewal moves the end date without touching a single term. List every party whose terms are absent, lapsed, or narrower than its processing, and name who will renegotiate, cut back what the party receives, or accept the position.

evidenceHint.en: Coverage sweep naming every party checked, the agreement version relied on, and each gap raised with an owner and a date.

templates.title: Interoperability and multi-party approaches
templates.description: Implements ID.DE-P4: Interoperability frameworks or similar multi-party approaches are used to manage data processing ecosystem privacy risks.

title.en: Decide which shared processing arrangements will run under a multi-party framework

description.en: Where three or more parties handle the same data, pairwise agreements leave the seams unowned: every pair is covered and the end-to-end outcome is nobody's. List the arrangements of that shape and name, for each, the framework, code of conduct, certification scheme or consortium rulebook it will run under. Where no suitable instrument exists, say so, name what carries the exposure instead, and who accepted that position.

evidenceHint.en: Schedule of multi-party arrangements with the chosen instrument beside each, and the accepted exceptions named.

title.en: Implement the interoperability framework's privacy provisions in each system exchanging data under it

description.en: Joining a framework changes nothing until the systems actually emit and honour what it specifies — purpose codes, consent or preference signals, retention markers, and the agreed way parties refer to the same individual. Work through every exchange the framework covers and set down, provision by provision, what is implemented, what a local equivalent stands in for, and what the organisation does not do at all. An unimplemented provision is a divergence to carry openly, with the person who accepted it, rather than an intention.

evidenceHint.en: Conformance profile per covered exchange, provision by provision, with the accepted divergence list and its approver.

title.en: Re-examine each multi-party arrangement against the framework version now in force

description.en: Frameworks are revised, participants join and leave, and a profile that conformed at signature quietly stops conforming without anyone being told. For each arrangement, compare what the organisation operates today against the published version currently in force, and check whether the parties named at the outset are still the parties involved. Record a decision for every divergence found — adopt the change, seek an exception, or withdraw from the arrangement — with the date it takes effect.

evidenceHint.en: Dated comparison note per arrangement listing the version reviewed, divergences found and the decision recorded for each.

templates.title: Routine assessment of ecosystem parties
templates.description: Implements ID.DE-P5: Ecosystem parties are routinely assessed using audits, test results, or other evaluations to confirm they are meeting their contractual, interoperability-framework, and other obligations.

title.en: Fix what counts as an acceptable evaluation, and how often each tier owes one

description.en: Routine re-assessment collapses without a stated bar: one party sends a current audit report, another a two-year-old certificate, a third a completed questionnaire it filled in itself, and all three are filed as evidence. Say which forms are acceptable — independent audit, penetration test result, certification against a named scheme, a supervised control test — and set the interval each exposure tier owes, so a lapsed evaluation is a date arithmetic rather than a judgement call. Name what happens when a party supplies nothing, because an interval with no consequence behind it is a reminder, not a control.

evidenceHint.en: The standard as issued: acceptable evaluation forms, the interval per exposure tier, and the stated consequence for a party that supplies none.

title.en: Obtain an independent evaluation for each high-priority party

description.en: Ask each high-priority party for whatever evidence of its conduct exists — an audit result, a test result, a certification, or another party's evaluation — and record what it showed measured against the obligations recorded for that party. Record refusals and non-responses as outcomes rather than leaving the entry blank.

evidenceHint.en: Per-party file holding the evaluation received, its date and source, and the assessor's note of which recorded obligations it did and did not address.

title.en: Decide the standing of each party whose evaluation is missing or stale

description.en: List the parties with no current evaluation and, for each, record the decision taken — chase, restrict what they receive, accept the gap, or end the engagement — with the person who took it. A party left undecided is the outcome this task exists to prevent.

evidenceHint.en: Decision list naming each party without a current evaluation, the decision taken, the decision-maker and the date.

templates.title: Privacy values and the conditions they set
templates.description: Implements GV.PO-P1: Organizational privacy values and policies (e.g., conditions on data processing such as data uses or retention periods, individuals' prerogatives with respect to data processing) are established and communicated.

title.en: Write down the organisation's privacy values and the conditions they place on processing

description.en: State the values the organisation holds about data, then translate each into concrete conditions that bind processing — what data may be used for, how long it may be held, and what an individual may ask of it. Values with no condition beneath them are a preamble, so pair each one with at least a condition someone could breach.

title.en: Set the retention period and permitted uses for each category of data held

description.en: A value binds nothing until it names data and a number, so take the categories from the processing inventory and write against each the period after which the data goes, the uses it may be put to, and the uses ruled out. Where two conditions land on the same category and disagree, an analysis wanting three years of history against a twelve-month deletion, decide which one governs now rather than leaving both on the page for whoever operates the system to choose between. A category left without a stated period is not neutral: in practice it defaults to keeping the data forever, so leave those rows visible with an owner named against them.

evidenceHint.en: Condition table listing each data category, the deletion point set for it, the uses allowed and refused, and the owner of any category still blank.

title.en: Find the processing that no stated condition governs

description.en: Coverage fails quietly: every condition on the page is about processing somebody remembered, so the set looks complete when read from the inside. Work from the data actions inventory instead, taking each recorded action, finding the condition that governs what it may be used for and how long its data is kept, and listing the actions where nothing does. This does not ask whether practice obeyed the conditions; it asks which processing has nothing to obey, because an action with no condition over it is settled in practice by whoever operates it.

evidenceHint.en: Coverage list naming each data action checked, the condition found over it, and the actions left with none.

templates.title: Instilling privacy values in development
templates.description: Implements GV.PO-P2: Processes to instill organizational privacy values within system/product/service development and operations are established and in place.

title.en: State what an exception must record before work proceeds against a privacy value

description.en: Every delivery process grants exceptions, and the ones granted verbally are indistinguishable afterwards from a value nobody applied. Fix what an exception has to capture — which condition is being set aside, for which piece of work, who authorised it, what compensates, and when it lapses — and put a ceiling on how long one may run unreviewed. Without a lapse date an exception becomes the new default, and the value survives only in the document nobody reads.

evidenceHint.en: The exception standard as issued, naming the fields an exception must carry, the authorising level, and the maximum period one may run before it is re-decided.

title.en: Record the means by which each privacy condition reaches development and operations

description.en: Take each condition written down beside the organisation's privacy values and record what carries it into the work of building and running systems — a standard or template it is written into, a default the platform already enforces, a question the change record asks, an approval that cannot be given without it — and for each name where a person doing that work meets it and who is accountable for keeping it there. A condition with nothing carrying it stays as a visible row with its owner named against it. This task records the carrier inside the work; instruction on what the conditions mean is delivered under the awareness control, and the data decision required at each life-cycle stage is recorded separately.

title.en: Test the delivery path with a change a privacy condition forbids

description.en: A route that has never refused anything looks identical to one nobody consults. Send a deliberate case through the normal path — a design, a ticket or a configuration change that plainly breaches one of the recorded conditions — and note which stage catches it, or that it reached release untouched. Run it on the real path with the usual reviewers rather than asking whether the step exists; what matters is where the work stopped, not that the step is written down.

evidenceHint.en: Dated account of the case put through, the route it travelled, the stage that rejected it or the point it reached unchallenged, and the change made to the path afterwards.

templates.title: Workforce privacy roles and responsibilities
templates.description: Implements GV.PO-P3: Roles and responsibilities for the workforce are established with respect to privacy.

title.en: Record the privacy responsibilities of each role and where they end

description.en: For every workforce role that touches data, state what it is responsible for doing and deciding, and state which of the adjacent responsibilities sit with an external party rather than with the role. Attach the resulting responsibility record, and name the role that resolves a boundary neither side claims.

title.en: Issue the privacy policy set to the workforce

description.en: Distribute the values, conditions and responsibility record to everyone bound by them, by whatever means the organisation uses to put a policy in front of staff, and record which version reached whom and when. This closes on the distribution record; instruction on what the responsibilities mean is delivered separately.

evidenceHint.en: Distribution record showing the policy version issued, the population it went to, and the date each part of that population received it.

title.en: Identify the privacy duties the current role map leaves unowned

description.en: A responsibility record is fixed against the role map of the day it was written, and then people leave, teams merge, posts are renamed and work is handed to a contractor, so a duty ends up recorded against a role nobody now holds — or split until two people each assume the other carries it. Work outward from the current staff and role list, naming the person accountable today for each recorded privacy responsibility, rather than reading the record and judging it plausible; a record that only looks coherent is exactly what decay produces. Catch the reverse case too, where staff are performing data actions from a role the record assigns no privacy responsibility at all, and settle each unowned duty on a named role instead of noting it.

evidenceHint.en: Per-responsibility check naming the role each duty is recorded against, who holds that role today, and every duty found with no accountable person together with where it was placed.

templates.title: Coordinating privacy roles internally and externally
templates.description: Implements GV.PO-P4: Privacy roles and responsibilities are coordinated and aligned with third-party stakeholders (e.g., service providers, customers, partners).

title.en: Map the privacy work that no single function or party completes alone

description.en: List the privacy activities that cannot be finished inside one function or one organisation, and for each name every holder of a piece — privacy, security, legal, a service provider, a customer, a partner. Start from the activities with a clock on them, because a seam only announces itself when a deadline runs across it. Skip this and the alignment work covers whichever seams somebody happened to remember, while the unclaimed ones stay invisible until a real case lands on them.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory of cross-boundary privacy activities naming the internal functions and external parties holding a piece of each, with those under a deadline marked.

title.en: Divide each shared privacy duty into the part each side performs

description.en: For every privacy activity that crosses a boundary, write down which steps the organisation performs, which the other party performs, what passes between them and by when — a contract saying a provider will "assist" names no step and so leaves the work unallocated. Do the same for the internal seams: privacy, security and legal each hold a piece of a breach assessment or an individual's request, and the piece none of them claims is the one that stalls. Put a named holder on each side of every split, with the deadline that attaches to their part. This captures the working split between the parties; the clause that obliges a party belongs in the requirements register, and instructing that party on what it means is delivered under the awareness control.

evidenceHint.en: Split sheet listing every cross-boundary activity, the steps allocated to each organisation or function, the named holder on both sides, and the deadline against each part.

title.en: Replay a case that crossed the boundary and find the step neither side took

description.en: An agreed split holds on paper until something actually travels across the seam. Take cases from the period that ran through more than one function or party — a request answered out of a provider's store, an incident first seen on a partner's side, a deletion that had to propagate outward — and reconstruct who did each step and at what point they knew it was theirs. A step done twice is as much a defect as a step nobody did, because both show the two sides were working from different splits. Raise the correction against the split itself and the counterparts named in it, not against the individual case.

evidenceHint.en: Reconstruction of each case examined, showing the sequence of steps, who carried out each one, and every gap or duplication found at the handover.

templates.title: Legal, regulatory and contractual requirements
templates.description: Implements GV.PO-P5: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding privacy are understood and managed.

title.en: Define the test that decides whether a privacy obligation binds the organisation

description.en: With no stated test, the register ends up being whatever the person compiling it already knew: the home statute goes in, a customer's processing addendum and a published certification commitment do not, and a duty that attaches because an individual lives somewhere else is never considered. Name the classes of source to be swept — statutes and regulations in each jurisdiction the organisation reaches, sector regimes, supervisory guidance, customer and supplier agreements, and commitments the organisation has made publicly — and the criterion that puts one inside the boundary or outside it. Name who rules on a contested reading as well, because two competent lawyers read the same clause differently and a register with no tie-breaker quietly carries both answers.

evidenceHint.en: Scope statement naming the jurisdictions, sectoral regimes and classes of agreement in the sweep, the criterion for inclusion, and the person who settles a disputed reading.

title.en: Compile the register of legal, regulatory and contractual privacy requirements that apply

description.en: List every legal, regulatory and contractual source that imposes a privacy requirement on the organisation, state in plain terms what each requires it to do, and name the internal policy or process that answers it. Where a requirement has nothing answering it, leave the row visible and name its owner.

title.en: Find the obligations that changed or arrived since the register was compiled

description.en: A requirement register decays from the outside in: the entries already written stay readable while a statute is amended, a regulator reissues its guidance, a customer contract is renegotiated at renewal, or the business opens in a market whose regime nobody has read. Work from the sources that know about change — horizon-scanning subscriptions, the contract renewal log, the period's new products and markets — because re-reading the register can only surface entries that are wrong, never obligations that were never entered. For each change decide whether it amends an entry, adds one, or retires one, and say which. This pass tests the statements of what is required, not whether the organisation is complying with them.

evidenceHint.en: Dated review note listing each amendment, new instrument, reissued guidance and renegotiated agreement picked up in the period, the source it came from, and the entry added, altered or withdrawn for it.

templates.title: Privacy risk in governance and risk management
templates.description: Implements GV.PO-P6: Governance and risk management policies, processes, and procedures address privacy risks.

title.en: Settle which enterprise risk documents and forums privacy must be written into

description.en: "Our risk framework already covers privacy" stays unfalsifiable until somebody names the documents, and each owner can point at another owner's procedure. Name the instruments in scope — the enterprise risk policy, the risk taxonomy, the risk committee's terms of reference, the risk acceptance procedure, the internal audit plan — and for each state what would count as covering privacy risk, because a passing mention is not coverage. Note the instruments deliberately left outside and why, so the check that follows works from a fixed list rather than an impression of what was meant to be included.

evidenceHint.en: Signed scoping note listing each in-scope instrument, its owner, the bar it must meet for privacy, and the exclusions with reasons.

title.en: Give privacy risk its own category, owner and entry in the enterprise risk register

description.en: A privacy risk kept on a list the privacy function maintains for itself never competes for money or attention against the risks executives already watch, and one filed under "compliance" or "IT" loses the thing that defines it — the harm lands on people rather than on the balance sheet. Open a privacy category in the enterprise risk taxonomy, raise entries there for the privacy risks already known, and give each an accountable owner drawn from the same population that owns every other entry. The awkward part is scoring: enterprise impact scales are written as loss to the organisation, so set down how harm to individuals is expressed on that scale, or privacy entries will be rated low by default and drop below the line that gets treated.

evidenceHint.en: Register export showing each privacy entry under its new category with a named owner, plus the written rule for scoring harm to individuals.

title.en: Confirm the organisation's governance and risk policies address privacy risk

description.en: Read the governance and risk-management policies that are not privacy-specific and record, for each, where privacy risk is addressed and where it is silent. Raise the change needed for each silence and name who will make it.

evidenceHint.en: Review note naming each governance or risk policy read, the privacy provision found in it, and the changes raised where none was found.

templates.title: Agreed risk management processes
templates.description: Implements GV.RM-P1: Risk management processes are established, managed, and agreed to by organizational stakeholders.

title.en: Define how a privacy risk is raised, decided and escalated

description.en: Write down who may raise a privacy risk, who may decide a response at each level of severity, what must escalate and to whom, and what happens when a decision is not taken. Attach the process description; it is the thing stakeholders are later asked to agree to.

title.en: Name the forum that decides a privacy risk and the authority each seat carries

description.en: A process is only as agreed as the people who can be held to it, so name the body that takes privacy risk decisions, who sits on it, and what each seat can commit — accept on behalf of a business line, fund a treatment, overrule a product date. State the quorum and what happens when it is not met, because a decision taken by whoever attended is the failure this requirement is about: the process was established, and then not managed. Record where a seat is vacant rather than letting the remaining members absorb it silently.

evidenceHint.en: Terms of reference for the deciding body: seats, the commitment each may make, quorum, the escalation when quorum fails, and any seat currently vacant.

title.en: Obtain agreement to the process and tolerance from the functions bound by them

description.en: Put the process description and tolerance statement to each function that has to apply them, and record each one's agreement or objection together with how objections were settled. An unanswered objection recorded is more useful than a signature that hides it.

evidenceHint.en: Agreement record naming each stakeholder function, the date, and any objection raised with its resolution.

title.en: Trace a sample of raised privacy risks through to the decision that closed them

description.en: Draw items from across the period, deliberately including ones nobody pressed for, and follow each from the moment it entered the register to the decision recorded against it: who decided, under what authority, and how long it waited before anyone did. A process can look healthy in aggregate while the items that embarrass someone are precisely the ones that never reach a decision, so the sample has to be drawn by the reviewer rather than offered up by the people running the register. Treat an item still open past the interval the process allows as a finding in its own right, not as work in progress, and note any decision taken by someone the process does not authorise to take it.

evidenceHint.en: Worked sample listing each item followed, the elapsed time from raising to resolution, the person who settled it, and the deviations found where authority or timing departed from the agreed route.

templates.title: Expressing organisational risk tolerance
templates.description: Implements GV.RM-P2: Organizational risk tolerance is determined and clearly expressed.

title.en: Settle what the privacy tolerance caps and whether it is read before or after controls

description.en: A tolerance means nothing until it is clear what it is applied to: the risk as it would stand with nothing mitigating it, or the risk left over once the controls the organisation actually runs are counted — the same sentence licenses very different processing under each reading. Decide that here, and decide whether the limit speaks to harm falling on individuals, exposure falling on the organisation, or two separate limits, because one figure covering both is always applied at its looser end. Write the decision down as the preamble the tolerance statement is then drafted against, so the level chosen later is not argued twice.

evidenceHint.en: Scoping note stating the measure the threshold applies to, whether mitigations are counted first, and whether harm to individuals and organisational exposure are held to separate limits.

title.en: Express the organisation's privacy risk tolerance in terms a ranked risk can be compared against

description.en: State what level of privacy risk the organisation will carry without further escalation and what it will not, using the same likelihood and impact terms in which risks are ranked, so a ranked risk can be placed against it without reinterpretation. A tolerance that cannot be compared to a ranking is a sentiment.

title.en: Compare recent risk decisions against the stated tolerance

description.en: Take the privacy risk decisions made since the last review and place each against the tolerance as written. Record every decision that fell outside it, whether it was escalated as the process requires, and what is being done about the ones that were not.

evidenceHint.en: Review note listing the decisions checked, the tolerance applied to each, and the decisions found outside tolerance with their escalation status.

templates.title: Tolerance informed by ecosystem role
templates.description: Implements GV.RM-P3: The organization's determination of risk tolerance is informed by its role in the data processing ecosystem.

title.en: Decide which parts of the organisation's ecosystem standing may move the tolerance

description.en: Before any threshold is written, name the facts about where the organisation sits that its tolerance has to answer to: the roles it holds in each relationship, whose data it handles and at what volume, whether those individuals had any real choice, and who else builds on its output. Say which of those may push the tolerance down and which are not permitted to push it up, because a derivation written after the number is chosen will find a reason for whatever was already wanted. List the facts deliberately left out with the reason for each, so a later reader can tell an omission from a decision.

evidenceHint.en: Scoping note listing each fact admitted as an input to the threshold, the direction it is allowed to push, and the ones excluded with reasons.

title.en: Record how the organisation's ecosystem role shaped that tolerance

description.en: For each role the organisation holds in the data processing ecosystem, explain why the tolerance sits where it does — a party acting on another's behalf carries a different exposure than one deciding for itself, and a party others depend on carries more than one that stands alone. Attach the reasoning to the tolerance statement.

title.en: Find the ecosystem roles the tolerance's justification never accounted for

description.en: Take the relationships opened, altered or inherited since the tolerance was last justified — a first processing mandate for a regulated client, a service other firms now build their own products on, a sub-processor engaged on the organisation's own initiative — and check whether the reasoning attached to the tolerance names each one. A justification written while the organisation processed only for itself keeps reading plausibly after it has become a party others depend on, because nothing in it names the role that moved. For each role the reasoning misses, record whether the tolerance stands as written, shifts, or is held open until the body that owns it decides.

evidenceHint.en: Dated note naming each role the organisation held during the period, whether the tolerance reasoning addressed it, and what was decided about the ones it missed.

templates.title: Workforce privacy awareness and training
templates.description: Implements GV.AT-P1: The workforce is informed and trained on its roles and responsibilities.

title.en: Identify the audiences needing privacy instruction and what each must be able to do

description.en: Separate the general workforce, senior executives, staff holding named privacy duties, and external parties, and for each record the responsibilities they must be able to carry out afterwards. Draw those responsibilities from the recorded role responsibilities and party obligations rather than restating generic privacy topics.

title.en: Deliver the instruction to each internal audience and record completion

description.en: Deliver to the workforce, the senior executives and the staff holding named privacy duties, by whatever means suits each, and record completion per person. Record separately, for the executive and privacy-duty audiences, what their session covered that the general one did not.

evidenceHint.en: Completion record per audience showing the names reached, the material version delivered, and the dates.

title.en: Check delivery against the audience list and follow up those not reached

description.en: Compare the completion and briefing records against the audience list, name every person and party still outstanding, and record the follow-up taken for each. Record anyone who cannot be reached and what is being done about their access instead.

evidenceHint.en: Gap list naming each outstanding recipient, the follow-up taken, and the position of anyone who remained unreached.

templates.title: Senior executives understand their roles
templates.description: Implements GV.AT-P2: Senior executives understand their roles and responsibilities.

title.en: Set the standard of privacy understanding required of the board and the executive team

description.en: Write down what a director or officer is expected to recognise, decide and answer for, and how that differs from the day-to-day practice the workforce is taught. Without that line drawn, the board assumes privacy is discharged by whoever holds the specialist title, while the specialist assumes risks were accepted at a level that never actually saw them. Name the posts the standard binds — board members, committee chairs, officers, and the directors of any subsidiary carrying its own statutory exposure — because personal liability follows the seat rather than the reporting line.

evidenceHint.en: Board-adopted statement of what a director or officer is expected to recognise, decide and answer for on privacy matters.

title.en: Walk each senior executive through the privacy decisions reserved to them

description.en: Take the decisions that cannot be settled below board or officer level — accepting a privacy risk that sits outside the stated tolerance, funding or cutting privacy work, approving a launch or an acquisition that changes what the organisation processes, authorising notification after a breach — and show each executive what signing one commits the organisation to and what they personally answer for afterwards. An executive who only sits through the workforce session learns handling rules they will never apply themselves and none of the choices that arrive solely at their level. Leave operational procedure out of it: the work is recognising a privacy decision when it arrives dressed as a budget line, a launch date or a deal.

evidenceHint.en: Dated briefing pack and attendance note for the board and officer session, listing each approval that cannot be signed at a lower level.

title.en: Question each executive on their privacy duties without the privacy team present

description.en: Accountability at this level is personal: a regulator's interview, an investor question or a journalist's call goes to the chief executive, and the organisation finds out at that moment whether the understanding was real or borrowed from a slide deck. Sit with each named executive alone and ask what processing would hurt people most if it went wrong, which privacy decision is currently theirs to take, and what they would do in the first hour of a breach. Deferring the answer to the privacy team is the finding, not a pass. Carry each gap into the next briefing rather than filing it with the attendance record.

evidenceHint.en: Notes from each one-to-one session naming the post held, the questions put, and the gaps carried into the next briefing.

templates.title: Privacy personnel understand their roles
templates.description: Implements GV.AT-P3: Privacy personnel understand their roles and responsibilities.

title.en: Draw the privacy specialists' instruction from the decisions that stop with them

description.en: Everyone else's privacy instruction ends in "raise it with the privacy function", which has nobody to pass it to — so list the questions that terminate there and make those the syllabus: assessing a newly proposed processing activity, ruling on the ground it relies on, judging whether a data set is disassociated enough to leave, calling a notification inside its deadline. Against each, name the depth its holder needs and the outside sources whose movement makes yesterday's answer wrong, so currency has something specific to track rather than a yearly refresher. Scoped as awareness instead, the specialist ends up fluent in the policy and unable to apply it to the one case nobody else is positioned to decide.

evidenceHint.en: Syllabus per named privacy duty listing the judgements it terminates, the depth required of its holder, and the legal or product sources tracked for change.

title.en: Prepare the instruction material for each audience

description.en: Produce material addressed to each audience's own responsibilities — what they decide, what they must not do, and who they escalate to — rather than one set of slides shown to everyone. Attach the material per audience and name who approved its content.

title.en: Re-test the privacy specialists against decisions whose correct answer has since changed

description.en: A specialist's knowledge fails at the edges that moved — a regulator's changed position, a processing pattern the product did not have last year, an obligation it has newly fallen under — not at the material learned once. Take decisions the privacy function actually made in the period where the right answer would now differ, put them back to each duty holder and to whoever covers the duty while the holder is away, and settle the correct answer from the source text rather than from what the holder says it is. A specialist answering as they did a year ago is current in attendance only, and nothing downstream catches it: the workforce escalated precisely because it could not judge the question itself.

evidenceHint.en: Dated re-test record naming each holder and stand-in questioned, the case put to them, the answer given, and the source-based position it was measured against.

templates.title: Third parties understand their roles
templates.description: Implements GV.AT-P4: Third parties (e.g., service providers, customers, partners) understand their roles and responsibilities.

title.en: Translate each third party's privacy clauses into instructions its own staff can follow

description.en: The entity that signs a data processing agreement is never the person holding an individual's deletion request at nine on a Tuesday morning, and a clause drafted to allocate liability tells that person nothing about what to do next.
