For each engagement, work the binding terms down into the short set of acts the other side's people must actually perform — what to do when someone asks them for their data, what they may not collect on our behalf, whom to call and inside how many hours on a suspected breach — written in their queues, their vocabulary and their clock rather than ours. Address each set to the function that touches the data and name a holder there, because material that lands only with the account team or the signatory reaches nobody who will ever use it.

evidenceHint.en: Per-engagement operating brief showing, for each act required of the counterparty's people, the contract term it derives from and the function it was addressed to.

title.en: Brief each external party on the privacy responsibilities it holds

description.en: Take the obligations recorded for each ecosystem party and put them to the people at that party who must act on them, through the channel that relationship uses. Record which party was briefed, what was covered and who received it, including parties that declined.

evidenceHint.en: Per-party briefing record naming the party, the responsibilities covered, the recipients and the date, including declined or unanswered briefings.

title.en: Route a test privacy request to each external party's front line, not its account manager

description.en: A signed agreement plus a relationship manager who says yes, our people know is not evidence that anyone on the floor recognises the request when it lands. Put a real-shaped one — an individual asking for their data, or a suspected-breach report — into the same inbox, portal or number a customer or subcontractor would actually reach, then follow it: who picked it up, whether they recognised what it was, and whether it came back inside the window the contract sets. This is the only lever available here, since the organisation cannot order a supplier's staff onto a course and cannot see its induction records; what it can do is observe behaviour and re-brief the function that dropped the request. Tell the party afterwards that the probe was a test, so the co-operation the next one depends on survives it.

evidenceHint.en: Probe log per party: channel used, date sent, who responded, elapsed time against the contracted window, and the re-brief raised where it went wrong.

templates.title: Ongoing re-evaluation of privacy risk
templates.description: Implements GV.MT-P1: Privacy risk is re-evaluated on an ongoing basis and as key factors, including the organization's business environment and data processing, change.

title.en: Define the changes that force privacy risk to be re-evaluated

description.en: List the events that require the risk assessment to be revisited — new or changed processing, a change of environment or party, a shift in the business, a problematic data action — and state who must be told when one occurs and within what the organisation itself sets. Attach the trigger list; it is what the later re-evaluations are measured against.

title.en: Take the current reading of every factor whose movement re-opens a risk assessment

description.en: A trigger list is unusable until every factor it names has a recorded value to compare against: nobody can say the processing volume, the jurisdictions, the vendor set or the population served has moved if the old state exists only in memory. Fix each factor's value on the day an assessment is signed off, store it with that assessment rather than in a register that ages on its own, and make it specific enough to compare mechanically, since a handful of EU customers cannot be tested against next year's figure. Include the factors that sit outside the organisation, such as the legal regime and the ecosystem position being relied on, because those move without anyone raising a change request.

evidenceHint.en: Dated snapshot filed against each signed-off assessment, giving the value of every watched factor at that moment and the source it was read from.

title.en: Re-evaluate privacy risk for each triggered change and record the outcome

description.en: When a listed trigger fires, revisit the affected part of the assessment and record what was reassessed, what changed in the ranking or responses, and what did not. Where a trigger fired and no re-evaluation followed, record that too, with the reason.

evidenceHint.en: Dated re-evaluation record naming the trigger, the processing reassessed, and the change made to the risk or its response.

title.en: Age the untouched privacy risk assessments and decide which must be redone

description.en: Trigger-driven re-evaluation has a blind spot where it looks safest: processing that nothing has happened to is never re-examined, while the ground under it shifts, as a regulator's interpretation hardens, the population grows, or a control quietly stops working. Order the standing assessments by the date each was last revisited, not by whoever has been asking about them, and send the oldest back through assessment on age alone with no trigger required. An assessment that has outlived the interval the organisation set for itself is a finding in its own right, not a scheduling problem to absorb.

evidenceHint.en: Ordered list of every standing assessment with its last-revisited date, the interval it was measured against, and the disposition recorded for each one past that interval.

templates.title: Reviewing values, policies and training
templates.description: Implements GV.MT-P2: Privacy values, policies, and training are reviewed and any updates are communicated.

title.en: Assemble the privacy material under review and every restatement of it in circulation

description.en: Gather the values statement, the privacy policies and standards, and the instruction material, then go one step further and find where those same rules are restated in someone else's words — a handbook section, an onboarding deck, an intranet answer, a contract annex, an induction quiz. Name the owner and the version of each, because a revision has to reach the restatements as well, and nobody maintains a copy they have not been told they hold. A review drawn up from the documents with privacy in the title leaves staff being taught last year's rule by material nobody counted.

evidenceHint.en: Register of the documents, modules and derived copies in scope, each with its owner, current version and the place it is published.

title.en: Rework the training material each privacy revision touches and reissue it to those already taught

description.en: When a rule is revised, the master document moves and everything downstream keeps teaching the old one — the induction deck, the quiz answers, the handbook paragraph, the slide a manager reuses. Work through the material tied to the revised rule, change what the revision actually changed, and mark the version now in force so a reader can tell which one they hold. Then put the change in front of the people who completed the earlier version: material updated only for new joiners leaves the population already taught confidently wrong.

evidenceHint.en: The superseded and replacement versions of each module or deck, with the date of issue and the roster of people re-taught against those who had completed the earlier version.

title.en: Review the privacy values, policies and instruction material and communicate what changed

description.en: Read them against what the organisation now does and against the problematic data actions handled since the last review, revise what no longer holds, and record what each change was for. Communicate the revisions to the people bound by them and record how.

evidenceHint.en: Change record showing each revision made, the trigger or incident behind it, and how the change was communicated.

templates.title: Assessing compliance with requirements
templates.description: Implements GV.MT-P3: Policies, processes, and procedures for assessing compliance with legal requirements and privacy policies are established and in place.

title.en: Translate each requirement and policy clause into a check with a pass condition

description.en: The register states each obligation in the language of the law or the contract, which is not yet something anyone can test. For every entry, and for every clause of the privacy policy set, name the artefact that would be inspected, the population a sample is drawn from, and the result that separates met from not met — settled before a pass runs, so a contested verdict is decided by the criterion rather than argued after the fact. Where no artefact could evidence an obligation, leave that visible on the row: it is a finding about the obligation, not a hole in the assessment.

evidenceHint.en: Assessment criteria sheet giving, for every register entry and privacy policy clause, the artefact to be inspected, the population sampled from it, and the result that counts as met.

title.en: Assess practice against the recorded requirements and privacy policies

description.en: Take the register of legal, regulatory and contractual requirements together with the privacy policy set, and check what the organisation currently does against each entry. Record the result per entry — met, not met, or unable to determine — and name the owner of every entry not met.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance assessment listing each requirement and policy checked, the result recorded against it, and the owner of each gap.

title.en: Re-test a sample of requirements and policy clauses last reported met

description.en: A failed entry gets an owner and a date; an entry marked met is never looked at again, so a wrong pass can stand for years. Draw a handful of the met verdicts — weighted towards the obligations that would hurt most if they were wrong — and re-derive each from practice itself rather than from the earlier assessor's note or the policy text that promises it. Count as well how many register entries and policy clauses the last pass never reached, because an assessment that touches only what is easy to evidence can report a clean run across a small fraction of what applies.

evidenceHint.en: Re-performance note naming the rows drawn, the evidence examined for each, any verdict that changed, and the count of register rows the earlier pass never touched.

templates.title: Communicating progress on privacy risk
templates.description: Implements GV.MT-P4: Policies, processes, and procedures for communicating progress on managing privacy risks are established and in place.

title.en: Draw every figure in the progress report from the register behind it

description.en: Name the register, tracker or log that each number and statement in the progress report comes from — risks re-ranked, responses closed, responses overdue, problems reported and answered — and pull this period's account from those sources rather than from whoever is writing it. A figure with no fixed source cannot be set beside last period's, so the report shows activity but never movement. Cut the version that goes to a customer, partner or supervisory body from the same registers as the internal one, or two accounts of the same quarter will circulate and differ.

evidenceHint.en: Reporting pack listing each figure issued, the source it was pulled from, and the period it covers.

title.en: Report progress on managing privacy risk to those who must act on it

description.en: Issue a report covering what changed in the risk picture, what responses closed, what is overdue and what was learned from reports received, to the people whose decisions depend on it. Record its distribution so silence can later be distinguished from never having been told.

evidenceHint.en: The report as issued, with its date and distribution list.

title.en: Trace each item reported as underway through the reports that followed

description.en: A progress report can convey motion for years by carrying the same response as in hand every period, with only the wording refreshed. Take the items the last several reports described as underway, find where each one stands in the register today, and mark those whose state has not moved across successive issues. Put the elapsed time in front of the recipients, because no single issue of a report can show it.

evidenceHint.en: Period-over-period comparison naming each item carried as underway, the issues it appeared in, and its state in the register today.

templates.title: Responding to problematic data actions
templates.description: Implements GV.MT-P5: Policies, processes, and procedures are established and in place to receive, analyze, and respond to problematic data actions disclosed to the organization from internal and external sources (e.g., internal discovery, researchers, individuals).

title.en: Draw the line between a disclosed privacy harm and an ordinary defect report

description.en: Reports that the organisation's own processing hurt someone do not arrive labelled: one lands in the security inbox as a vulnerability, one in support as an angry ticket, one in an engineer's message saying the export looked wrong. Write the test a triager applies — a person is worse off because of what was done with data about them, whether or not any system misbehaved — and name the queues, addresses and internal channels read against it, including the ones outsiders use without being invited. State that anything matching the test leaves the queue it landed in rather than being closed by whoever fixed the bug, because a fix answers what the system did and never who it reached.

evidenceHint.en: The triage test as issued, the list of inbound channels and addresses it is applied to, and a sample of recent items classified under it.

title.en: Establish which individuals a disclosed data action reached and over what period

description.en: A disclosure names a symptom — one exposed record, one misdirected export, one screen showing another person's details — and the first job is to find the boundary of what it describes: who was actually touched, from when, and how many times it repeated. Reconstruct that from the logs and the data itself rather than from the reporter's account, which is bounded by what a single person happened to see, and keep the query or extract that produced the answer. Where the records cannot settle a date or a count, write that down as unproven; a scope recorded as unknown can be re-opened, while one quietly narrowed to what was easy to demonstrate cannot. Everything that follows — halting the action, repairing the records, deciding who must be told — is sized against the reach settled here.

evidenceHint.en: Per-disclosure finding: the affected population with the query or extract behind it, the first and last dates the action ran, and every figure the records could not settle marked unproven.

title.en: Re-examine the disclosures dismissed as no harm against what the logs show

description.en: The cheapest way to close a report is to conclude nothing happened, and that verdict is the one nobody audits: disclosures that led to work leave a trail of their own, while a dismissal leaves one sentence. Take every report closed over the period as no harm, unreproducible, or working as intended, and have someone other than the original analyst check the stated reason against the records it should have been drawn from. Count how many were later raised again by a different source — a second person reporting something already written off is the plainest sign the first reading was wrong.

evidenceHint.en: Dated re-read of every closure claiming nothing happened in the period, naming the second reader, the records checked against each, and the verdicts overturned.

templates.title: Lessons learned from problematic data actions
templates.description: Implements GV.MT-P6: Policies, processes, and procedures incorporate lessons learned from problematic data actions.

title.en: Settle what separates a one-off slip from a rule that must be rewritten

description.en: State the test that decides whether an event teaches anything: a person departing from a rule that was clear and workable says little about the rule, whereas an event the rule allowed, or one nobody could have complied with as written, says a great deal. Name the documents a lesson is permitted to reach — the privacy policy set, operating procedures, design standards, retention schedules, contract templates and instruction material — so an amendment cannot land somewhere nobody is bound by. Without the test the standing verdict becomes human error and retraining, which closes the file before anyone asks whether the rule could have been followed at all.

evidenceHint.en: Approved criterion with a worked example on each side of the line, plus the list of amendable documents and the person empowered to change each.

title.en: Carry each confirmed lesson into the procedure people work from

description.en: A lesson that lives only in the incident write-up changes nothing: the write-up is read once and filed, while the operating text consulted at the moment of the work still says what it said before the harm. Amend the document that governs the step, and accept that some lessons are subtractions rather than additions — a field no longer collected, a default turned off, a standing permission withdrawn. Cite the originating event beside the amended clause, because a rule with no visible reason is the first thing a later editor tidies away. Where a lesson was answered with a briefing instead of a change to the text, say so: a briefing leaves nothing behind once the people change.

evidenceHint.en: The amended document at its new version, showing each clause added, altered or struck, the date it took effect, and the event reference recorded against it.

title.en: Walk each handled harm through the procedure as it now reads

description.en: An amendment can answer the write-up and still leave the event free to happen again, because the new wording addresses what was reported rather than the step that permitted it. Take the problematic data actions handled since the last pass, follow each original sequence through the text as it now stands, and name the clause that would halt it — or record that nothing would. Put the number of events that produced a documented change beside the period's total, since events closed without touching any document are invisible when only the amendments are listed. Treat a harm that recurred after its lesson was folded in as evidence the wrong cause was addressed.

evidenceHint.en: Per-event trace listing the original sequence, the clause in current text that would now stop it, and the period total shown against the count of events that altered no document.

templates.title: Complaints, concerns and questions
templates.description: Implements GV.MT-P7: Policies, processes, and procedures for receiving, tracking, and responding to complaints, concerns, and questions from individuals about organizational privacy practices are established and in place.

title.en: Set the answer owed to a complaint, a concern and a question

description.en: The three arrive through the same door and are not the same thing: a question wants an answer, a concern wants someone to look and say what they found, a complaint wants a decision and a route onward if the person rejects it. Write down, for each, what must reach the individual, the outer limit they wait, and the holding acknowledgement that goes out while the substantive answer is still being prepared. State who may close a contact with nothing sent back and on what grounds — silent closure is the failure this requirement exists to prevent, and it stays invisible unless the permitted grounds are named beforehand.

evidenceHint.en: The agreed standard as written: each kind of contact, what goes back to the individual, the outer time limit, and the named grounds on which one may be closed with nothing sent.

title.en: Define the intake routes for reported problems and individuals' complaints

description.en: Write down, for the two populations separately, how a report of a problematic data action from a staff member, researcher or member of the public arrives and how a complaint, concern or question from an individual arrives; where each lands, who analyses it, what response is owed and how it is tracked to a close. Attach the procedure and the contact points it publishes.

title.en: Read the replies sent to individuals who complained in the period

description.en: Take the complaints, concerns and questions closed since the last review and read what actually went back to the person: whether it addressed the matter they raised, in words they can use, and whether anything left the organisation at all before the item was marked closed. Count the individuals who made contact a second time about the same matter, because a repeat contact is the person's own verdict on the first reply and it is the one measure that does not rest on the handler's opinion of their own work. Where a closure carries no outbound message, name the item and whoever closed it rather than quietly adjusting the count, and say whether the substance was refused, deferred or simply forgotten.

evidenceHint.en: Sample of items closed in the period showing the outbound message on each, the date it left, every closure with no message at all, and the number of people who made contact a second time about the same matter.

templates.title: Authorising, maintaining and revoking data processing

description.en: Implements CT.PO-P1: Policies, processes, and procedures for authorizing data processing (e.g., organizational decisions, individual consent), revoking authorizations, and maintaining authorizations are established and in place.

title.en: Define what makes a data action authorised and how an authorisation ends

description.en: State the bases on which the organisation authorises processing — an organisational decision, an individual's agreement, or another basis — and, for each, what must be recorded when an authorisation is given, how it is withdrawn, and what processing must stop when it is. Attach the resulting procedure covering the whole life of an authorisation, not just its grant.

title.en: Bind each data action in the inventory to the authorisation that permits it

description.en: Work through the processing the organisation actually performs and, against each one, name the authorisation it runs under, the limits that authorisation carries, and the date or event at which it lapses. Without that binding an action continues simply because nobody stopped it, and a withdrawal has no target — the decision exists on paper while no one can say which processing it was meant to end. Attach the binding at the level the action is performed rather than at system level, since one system commonly runs several actions resting on different grounds. Where an action cannot be traced to any authorisation, leave the entry standing and unresolved instead of blank, because that gap is the finding.

evidenceHint.en: Authorisation map listing every performed processing activity, the decision or agreement it rests on, the limits attached to it, its lapse date or triggering event, and any activity left untraced.

title.en: Check a sample of performed actions against the written procedures

description.en: Take a sample of data reviews, transfers, disclosures, alterations, deletions and individual requests actually carried out, and compare what was done with what the procedure says. Record each divergence, whether the outcome was still correct, and the procedure step that was skipped or unclear.

evidenceHint.en: Sample review naming the actions examined, the procedure step each was measured against, and every divergence found with its consequence.

templates.title: Procedures for review, transfer, alteration and deletion

description.en: Implements CT.PO-P2: Policies, processes, and procedures for enabling data review, transfer, sharing or disclosure, alteration, and deletion are established and in place (e.g., to maintain data quality, manage data retention).

title.en: Gather the occasions that oblige the organisation to check, correct, hand over or clear data

description.en: Procedures only ever stretch as far as the occasions they were written for, and a list drawn from what the systems already do quietly omits the awkward ones. Work outward from the retention schedule, contracts that end, quality checks that turn up wrong records, provider exits and divestments, because each names a moment when held data has to be looked at, put right, passed on or got rid of. Put down the occasions nobody handles today as well: those are what the written procedure has to close rather than describe. Tie each occasion to the holdings it reaches, so the drafting that follows has a denominator instead of a wish list.

evidenceHint.en: Schedule of handling occasions, each with the obligation or business event behind it, the holdings it reaches, and a marker where nothing is in place today.

title.en: Write the procedure for reviewing, transferring, sharing, altering and deleting data

description.en: For each of those actions, record who may request it, who may perform it, what must be checked before it happens, and what is written down afterwards. Include what is done when the action cannot be completed as requested, so an incomplete action has a defined outcome rather than none.

title.en: Ask someone who did not write the steps to run a transfer and an erasure

description.en: A procedure can be complete on paper and still leave the organisation unable to act, because the one person who has done it before supplies the missing half from memory and nobody notices the text is short. Pick a holding, hand the written steps to someone who took no part in drafting them, and have them perform a transfer out and an erasure with no spoken help, noting every point where they had to stop and ask. Vary which of the handling steps is exercised each period so review and correction are covered too. Where the reader could not finish, the defect belongs to the text and the wording is what gets changed.

evidenceHint.en: Dated walkthrough record naming the holding used, the person who followed the text unaided, each question they had to ask, and the wording amended afterwards.

description.en: Implements CT.PO-P3: Policies, processes, and procedures for enabling individuals' data processing preferences and requests are established and in place.

title.en: Set out the preferences and requests individuals may make and the time limit on each

description.en: Name every choice a person can express and every ask they can put to the organisation, say which are honoured as of right and which are discretionary, and fix how long each has to be answered in. Without this list, staff decide case by case and the promise made in public drifts away from what the procedure can actually deliver. Settle here who may act for someone else, since a parent, executor or appointed agent arrives with no obvious place in an unscoped process.

evidenceHint.en: Approved catalogue listing each choice and ask available to a person, its status as obligatory or discretionary, its answering deadline, and who may raise one on another's behalf.

title.en: Write the procedure for handling an individual's preference or request

description.en: Record how a request or a stated preference is received, how the requester is established as the person concerned, how the data in scope is located across the inventory, what outcome is given back to them, and what is retained about the exchange. Cover the case where the request cannot be met and what the individual is told instead.

title.en: Revisit an older accepted preference against how that person is treated today

description.en: A stated preference is a standing instruction, not a ticket that closes. Pick individuals whose preference was accepted in an earlier period and look at what happens to them now, because a restored backup, a reimported marketing list or a newly bought system quietly reinstates the processing they declined and nothing in the case file says so. Judge the outcome by the person's present treatment, not by the note recording that the request was actioned.

evidenceHint.en: Dated sample of individuals whose choice was accepted at least one period ago, showing the present state of processing for each and every case where it had drifted back.

templates.title: Data life cycle aligned to the system development life cycle

description.en: Implements CT.PO-P4: A data life cycle to manage data is aligned and implemented with the system development life cycle to manage systems.

title.en: Name the delivery routes the joined life cycle must govern

description.en: Systems arrive by more routes than the formal development process: a purchased subscription, a spreadsheet grown into a service, a model pipeline stood up by an analyst, a platform inherited with an acquisition. Set down each route by which a system can enter service, be materially changed or be withdrawn, name who controls each route, and mark which of them the alignment will bind. A route left off this list is one where no decision about data is ever owed, and no later inspection of the development process will notice its absence.

evidenceHint.en: Route list naming each way a system can enter service, be materially changed or be withdrawn, its controlling owner, and whether the alignment binds it.

title.en: Attach the data life cycle to the way systems are built, changed and retired

description.en: At each stage of the organisation's own approach to building and changing systems, state what must be decided about the data the system will hold — where it comes from, what it may be used for, how long it stays, and what happens to it when the system goes. Attach the amended life-cycle description showing the data decision required at each stage.

title.en: Trace last period's launches, changes and retirements back to their data decisions

description.en: Take the period's go-lives, material changes and decommissionings from the change and procurement records rather than from the privacy team's own file, and for each one find the stage that was supposed to produce a decision about the data and read what was actually recorded there. Retirement is where the alignment usually breaks: the system is switched off on schedule while its exports, backups and downstream copies carry on, because settling the fate of the data was never a condition of shutting it down. Write down every case where the decision came late, was taken outside the process, or was never taken at all, and name the stage that let it pass.

evidenceHint.en: Dated trace-back covering every system brought into service, materially changed or withdrawn in the period, naming the stage that owed each decision and what was recorded at it.

templates.title: Access to data elements for review

description.en: Implements CT.DM-P1: Data elements can be accessed for review.

title.en: Record which data actions each store supports today

description.en: For every store holding data in the inventory, record whether a record can be retrieved for review, released for transmission or disclosure, altered, and deleted, and who is able to perform each. Where one of those cannot be done, record it as a gap with a named owner rather than leaving the cell empty.

title.en: Decode the values a review retrieval returns into readable text

description.en: A store can return a row and still leave a reader with nothing usable: enumerations arrive as integers, references arrive as keys into other tables, and whole answers sit inside uploaded documents, free-text notes and log lines that an identifier-keyed query never opens. Build the lookup that resolves each returned value into the wording a person sees, and extend the retrieval to the elements that live outside the columns it selects. Name the elements for which no resolution exists, because a value that comes back as an opaque identifier has been retrieved but not made reviewable.

evidenceHint.en: Mapping from each stored code, key and document field to the wording a person sees, with every element that still resolves to nothing named.

title.en: Check a completed retrieval for gaps and values a reader cannot interpret

description.en: State how many elements the inventory says are held for that category of individual and how many came back, so a shortfall is visible instead of assumed away; an empty section usually means a join that matched nothing rather than data that was never held. Give the reading to whoever would use the output in earnest, since the person who built the retrieval reads past codes and abbreviations without noticing them. Write down each value the reader could not make sense of and each element found to be held somewhere the retrieval never reached.

evidenceHint.en: Read-back record naming the store and record used, the count of elements expected beside the count returned, and each value the reader could not make sense of.

templates.title: Access to data elements for transmission or disclosure

description.en: Implements CT.DM-P2: Data elements can be accessed for transmission or disclosure.

title.en: Decide which elements leave with an individual and which are held back

description.en: Settle, before anyone writes a query, which elements go out with a person and which are stripped: derived and inferred attributes, free-text notes and uploaded files, and anything carrying a second individual, another party's confidential material or the organisation's own internal analysis. Name who rules on a contested field and where that ruling is written down, or the same argument is re-fought on each request and answered differently every time. Left open, composition falls to whoever happens to run the query that day, and the organisation gives away too much in one case and a fraction of the record in the next.

evidenceHint.en: Signed composition rule listing the fields released, the categories withheld and why, plus the named arbiter for a disputed field.

title.en: Extract one individual's records from every store into a form the recipient can open

description.en: Every store holding the elements needs a way to return one named person's records on demand — a parameterised query, an export narrowed to a single key, a vendor ticket, or a written manual pull where nothing else exists. The stores with no export feature are the ones that decide whether a disclosure can happen at all, so the SaaS reachable only through its own screens, the archive and the message queue belong on the list as first-class entries rather than exceptions to settle later. Land the results in one package the receiving party can read without any of our software, and note for each store who performs the pull, what identifier it keys on and how long it takes — a path nobody can run inside the promised turnaround is a gap wearing the word manual.

evidenceHint.en: Per-store register naming the mechanism used, the person who runs it, and the elapsed time to produce a named subject's data.

title.en: Open an extract already disclosed and find whose data travelled with it

description.en: Take something the organisation genuinely sent in the period — a response issued to an individual, a file passed to an insurer, a feed handed to a partner — and read what left field by field against the person it was for. Two defects live in there and neither shows on the request ticket: rows or free-text belonging to somebody else that a join dragged along, and stores whose route returned empty so quietly that nobody noticed they contributed nothing. A package that looks complete is usually reporting the stores that answered, so count the contributing stores against the register rather than trusting the file's size.

evidenceHint.en: Field-level examination of one real outbound payload, naming every record belonging to someone else and every store that returned nothing.

templates.title: Access to data elements for alteration

description.en: Implements CT.DM-P3: Data elements can be accessed for alteration.

title.en: Establish which stored copy of a value a correction changes first

description.en: For each element, list the places it is held and say which of them a correction is applied to; the others must take their value from that one rather than be edited on their own. A correction written into a derived copy disappears the moment that copy is rebuilt from source, so the choice has to be settled before anyone is asked to make corrections. Flag any holding that cannot be overwritten at all — a signed document, an append-only ledger, a supplier's read-only interface — since those need a superseding entry and a reader that honours it. Note too the elements other records point at by value, where putting one right is not a single-field edit.

evidenceHint.en: Per-element list showing every place it is held, which holding a change is applied to, which ones take their value from that holding, and the holdings that cannot be overwritten with the route agreed for each.

title.en: Carry a corrected value into every cache, index and report fed from it

description.en: Changing the value at source does not change what a search index, a cached list or last night's aggregate serves; each keeps the old figure until something makes it rebuild. For every copy named in the scope, state what triggers it to take the change and the longest it may lag, and give the operator a way to force it when a correction cannot wait for the schedule. Two-way syncs need the most care: a reconciliation job that treats the far side as authoritative will quietly put the wrong value back, and the correction will look as though it never held.

evidenceHint.en: Propagation note listing each downstream copy, the trigger that makes it take a change at source, the longest it may lag, and the manual override available when it cannot wait.

title.en: Alter a live value and check which copies still serve the old one

description.en: Pick an element that is genuinely held in more than one place, correct it by the route people actually use, then query each copy for the previous value instead of trusting the design. Record how long each took to agree, and treat a copy that never agreed as a defect in the route rather than a quirk of the exercise. A correction that lasts only until the next rebuild or sync is worse than one refused outright, because nobody is told it came undone.

evidenceHint.en: Walkthrough record naming the element changed, the store it was changed in, each copy queried afterwards, the lag observed, and any copy still holding the superseded figure.

templates.title: Access to data elements for deletion

description.en: Implements CT.DM-P4: Data elements can be accessed for deletion.

title.en: Settle what counts as deleted rather than hidden, and which copies must be gone

description.en: Most systems can hide a record instantly and remove it slowly, so the word means one thing to a flag on the row, another to a tombstone in a replica, another again to an entry in a search index or a tape in a vault. Fix that standard before anyone builds against it: which stores must hold nothing at all, which may carry a tombstone and for how long, and what lag is accepted for an archive that is only overwritten on its own cycle. Without the line drawn, a soft-delete flag passes as removal and the gap surfaces only when a restore or a data export produces the record whole.

evidenceHint.en: Written standard stating the end state required of each class of store and the longest period a residual copy may survive.

title.en: Build a removal route into each store, including the ones that cannot delete in place

description.en: A deletion capability is only as good as its weakest store: the transactional database has a delete statement, while the search index, the event log, the analytics warehouse and the object archive frequently have none, so a row removed from the first survives intact in all the rest. For every store holding the element, implement the operation that actually takes it out — a delete, an index purge, a compaction that drops the key, or destruction of the key material where the bytes themselves cannot be rewritten — and write down which of those each store relies on. Where nothing can remove it before a retention window closes, say so plainly instead of letting a hidden row pass as a removal.

evidenceHint.en: Per-store table naming the operation that takes one individual's data out, with any store that can only be emptied by expiry marked as such.

title.en: Check whether deleted records returned through a restore, a replica or an upstream feed

description.en: Deletion is the data action most easily undone by routine operations nobody thinks of as writes. A backup taken before the removal and restored afterwards, a replica that was detached when the delete propagated, and a nightly feed from a source system that was never told all put the same record back, and the returning copy looks like an ordinary insert. Take the identifiers removed during the period and search for them in the systems restored, rebuilt or re-synchronised since, rather than re-running the deletion that reported success at the time.

evidenceHint.en: Period check listing the identifiers removed, the systems restored or re-synchronised since, and any record found alive again with the action taken.

templates.title: Destruction of data according to policy

description.en: Implements CT.DM-P5: Data are destroyed according to policy.

title.en: Wire each store's retention expiry to a destruction run that leaves nothing recoverable

description.en: A delete path that nobody calls is not destruction: data whose retention condition expired sits on, and the policy is honoured only for the records someone happens to ask about. For each store, connect the expiry to something that fires on its own, and pick a technique whose result the platform cannot reverse — overwriting the row is not enough where soft-delete windows, snapshots, replicas and object versioning will hand it back. Name the stores the automated path covers and the ones still needing a person, so the manual cases stay visible rather than being assumed handled.

evidenceHint.en: Per-store configuration or runbook naming what fires the destruction, the technique applied, and the recovery features closed off or accepted.

title.en: Record each destruction of data against the condition that required it

description.en: When data is destroyed, record what was destroyed, the store it left, the retention condition or request that required it, who performed it and when. Include destructions that were attempted and could not be completed, with what remains.

evidenceHint.en: Destruction record naming the data and store, the condition or request that required it, the performer and the date, including incomplete destructions.

title.en: Find the data still held past the point its destruction was due

description.en: Measure from the store, not from the destruction log: the log is written by whoever performed a destruction and says nothing at all about one that was never attempted. Query each store for the oldest surviving item in each data category and compare it against the point at which the policy obliged its destruction, then repeat that against the backups, exports, warehouse copies and non-production environments holding the same data under a different name. Every survivor is either a destruction that never ran or a copy nobody counted as a store, and those two need different fixes.

evidenceHint.en: Dated query output per store naming the oldest surviving item in each category, the date its destruction fell due, and the disposition of every survivor found.

description.en: Implements CT.DM-P6: Data are transmitted using standardized formats.

title.en: Select the interchange standards each class of transfer will use

description.en: Group the transfers by what they carry and who receives them — regulatory returns, partner feeds, portability copies handed to individuals, replication between the organisation's own systems — and settle on one published specification per group, before every integration picks its own and three dialects have to be kept alive. Write down what disqualifies a candidate: a format nobody maintains outside these walls, or one with no way for a payload to declare which version it follows. Name the transfers deliberately left outside this decision and what keeps them out, so conformance is later measured against a known population rather than whatever happens to be looked at.

evidenceHint.en: Signed decision listing each group of transfers, the specification chosen for it, the tests a candidate had to pass, and the transfers held outside scope.

title.en: Bind each data exchange to a named specification and version

description.en: For every route on which records leave or enter a system, name the published specification its payloads follow, the version of that specification in force, and the encoding and character set used, then change the sender to emit precisely that rather than whatever its library produces by default. Two endpoints can both claim the same standard and still disagree about dates, repeated elements or optional fields, so a version left unstated is not really a standard at all. Where a counterparty insists on a layout of its own, hold it as a named departure with an owner and an expiry, so the exceptions stay countable rather than quietly becoming the norm.

evidenceHint.en: Register of inbound and outbound routes, each naming the published standard, the release in force, the encoding, and any approved local departure with its end date.

title.en: Parse a captured payload against the specification the route declares

description.en: Take a message off a live route exactly as it was sent and run it through a validator obtained from the standard's maintainer, not the library the sending team already uses; a sender and its own parser agree with each other even when both are wrong. That the receiving system accepted the traffic proves nothing either, because integrations quietly grow a tolerance for one partner's quirks. Note every structural error, every element the specification does not define, and every field where a coded value has been replaced by free text, since those are the points at which a new recipient would fail.

evidenceHint.en: Validator output for a real message pulled from each sampled route, listing the structural errors, undefined elements and free-text substitutions it reported.

templates.title: Processing permissions carried with the data

description.en: Implements CT.DM-P7: Mechanisms for transmitting processing permissions and related data values with data elements are established and in place.

title.en: Decide which permission values must accompany a record and on which exchanges

description.en: Name the exchanges bound by this rule and the values each one must carry with the data: the authorisation relied on, the purposes allowed, how long it may be held, whether it may be passed on again, and when the permission lapses. Left unsettled, the first interface built sets an accidental precedent and every later one carries a different subset, leaving each recipient to guess at whatever is absent. Write down the exchanges deliberately excluded and the reason, so a gap is a decision somebody made rather than an oversight nobody noticed.

evidenceHint.en: Agreed decision listing the in-scope exchanges, the values required on each, and the reasoning recorded for every exclusion.

title.en: Record how processing permissions and the agreed form travel with data between systems

description.en: For each place where data elements leave one system for another, record what conveys the permissions and related values that govern them, the form the data itself is sent in and who agreed that form, and what the receiving side is expected to do with the permissions. Where nothing is conveyed, record that explicitly and name who carries the resulting risk.

title.en: Find the transfers where the data arrived and the permissions did not

description.en: Look at the receiving end rather than the sending one: an interface that silently drops a field it does not recognise still reports a successful hand-off, so the sender's log shows every record delivered while the recipient holds data it treats as carrying no restriction at all. Take the period's hand-offs, pull a sample of records as each recipient now stores them, and compare the permission values sitting there against what was attached at source. Count a permission that landed and was then overwritten by a local default as the same defect as one that never landed, because either way the recipient is processing on an assumption nobody made.

evidenceHint.en: Per-recipient sample naming each hand-off examined, the values attached at source, what the recipient held on inspection, and how every discrepancy was closed.

templates.title: Audit and log records under data minimisation

description.en: Implements CT.DM-P8: Audit/log records are determined, documented, implemented, and reviewed in accordance with policy and incorporating the principle of data minimization.

title.en: Choose the events that must leave an audit record behind

description.en: Logging otherwise accretes by default: a platform emits whatever its framework happens to emit, so the entries that would answer a later question about who touched personal data are either buried in noise or were never written at all. Name the processing events that must produce a record — those a privacy question cannot be answered without, plus any a statute or contract compels — and state which systems are in scope and which are deliberately excluded. Settling the event list first gives the field-level work a fixed population to justify rather than an open-ended one.

evidenceHint.en: Approved schedule of loggable events, the systems in scope, the obligation or question behind each entry, and the exclusions agreed.

title.en: Define what each processing log records and justify every field held

description.en: For each log kept about data processing, record which events it captures, which fields each entry carries, why each field is necessary for the purpose the log serves, and how long entries are held. Remove the fields that survive no justification, and record who reads the log and when it is looked at.

title.en: Separate the logs actually read from those merely retained

description.en: A stream that is collected, stored and never opened reads exactly like a reviewed one in any summary — both are present, both sit inside retention, and neither shows a reader. Walk the streams the logging policy says must be looked at and produce, for each, dated proof that someone looked: who, which window, and what they raised. Treat a stream with no reviewer against it as a finding in its own right, because a clean review and an absent review both come back empty.

evidenceHint.en: Per-stream schedule of completed reviews for the period naming each reviewer, the window covered, what they raised, and every stream with nobody against it.

description.en: Implements CT.DM-P9: Technical measures implemented to manage data processing are tested and assessed.

title.en: Derive a test for each technical measure and name the result that would fail it

description.en: Go through the technical measures the organisation relies on to manage processing and write, for each, the action to perform, the state it should leave behind, and the observation that would count as a failure. A test with no failing outcome written down can only ever pass, so the measures nobody can describe a failure for are the ones to draft first. Drive each through the same path a user or calling system would take rather than an administrative console, because the console can return success while the measure behind it does nothing.

evidenceHint.en: Test set listing every measure relied on, the steps to exercise it, the expected state, and the observation that would count as a failure.

title.en: Test the data actions and permission arrangements on a real record

description.en: Exercise the technical measures the organisation relies on — retrieving, releasing, altering and deleting a record, and conveying its permissions onward — using a real or representative record, and record the expected and observed outcome of each. Record the measures that could not be exercised and why.

evidenceHint.en: Test record naming each measure exercised, the store and record used, the expected outcome, the observed outcome and any measure left untested.

title.en: Count the technical measures no test touched, and re-aim the tests that outlived their subject

description.en: Take the register of technical measures as it stands now, not the list the tests were written from, and mark every measure that nothing exercised during the period — an empty result reads as a pass and hides the measures nobody thought to try. Then read each test that did run against the measure it claims to cover, because a measure since reconfigured or replaced keeps its old test passing against behaviour it no longer has. Name an owner for each measure left unexercised and each test whose subject has moved.

evidenceHint.en: Period comparison naming the measure register used as the denominator, each measure left unexercised, and every test found aimed at behaviour its measure no longer has.

description.en: Implements CT.DM-P10: Stakeholder privacy preferences are included in algorithmic design objectives and outputs are evaluated against these preferences.

title.en: Settle which automated decisions fall in scope and whose privacy preferences bind them

description.en: List the automated decisions and inferences this control covers, and against each one the groups whose privacy preferences its design objectives must answer to. Those groups run wider than the people whose data trains or feeds the model: the individuals the outputs are applied to hold preferences as well, and many will never have touched the system. Where a model is left out, record the reason and the person who agreed it, so the omission can be argued with later rather than discovered.

evidenceHint.en: Scope list of the automated decisions covered, the stakeholder groups attached to each, and every model excluded with its reason and the person who agreed.

title.en: Record the privacy preferences built into algorithmic design objectives

description.en: Where processing produces automated decisions or inferences, record the privacy preferences stakeholders hold, how each was turned into a design objective, and how the outputs were compared against those objectives. Record the comparisons that failed as well as those that passed, with what changed as a result.

title.en: Examine what each algorithm produced against the preferences its objectives carry

description.en: Pull the outputs a model actually produced over the period and hold each recorded preference up against them, rather than re-reading the design note that states it. A model retrained on fresher data can drift away from a preference its objectives still claim, and the objective itself will not announce the drift. Record every divergence found together with the decision taken on it: the model changed, its use narrowed, or the divergence accepted and why. Accepted divergences written down as plainly as corrected ones are what let the next reader tell an honoured preference from a quietly abandoned one.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison note naming the period and the outputs examined, each preference tested against them, every divergence found, and the decision recorded on each.

description.en: Implements CT.DP-P1: Data are processed to limit observability and linkability (e.g., data actions take place on local devices, privacy-preserving cryptography).

title.en: Record the disassociation applied to each data action so identified

description.en: For every action marked as not needing full identification, record what is actually done to limit identification, linkage or observability, and what identifying material still remains after it. The remaining material is the part a later re-association test is aimed at, so record it precisely rather than as a reassurance.

title.en: Test whether a disassociated data set can be linked back to an individual

description.en: Take a data set the organisation treats as disassociated and attempt, using material the organisation itself holds or could obtain, to link it back to a person. Record what was achievable, what was not, and what the attempt reveals about the residual recorded earlier.

evidenceHint.en: Test record naming the data set, the material used in the attempt, the outcome, and the residual identification found.

title.en: Revisit who can watch each data action and what it can now be joined against

description.en: Observability widens quietly: an action that once ran on the user's own device is moved to a shared service, a log gains a new reader, a feed acquires an intermediary, and a newly arrived data set makes two previously separate records matchable. For each action the organisation treats as limited, name every party that can see it take place today and every holding it could be matched against, then set that beside the position recorded when the limitation was put in. Where either has widened, state whether an owner accepted the widening or it simply happened unnoticed.

evidenceHint.en: Review note listing, per action, the parties with visibility today, the holdings it could be matched against, and whether any widening was accepted by a named owner.

description.en: Implements CT.DP-P2: Data are processed to limit the identification of individuals (e.g., de-identification privacy techniques, tokenization).

title.en: Identify the data actions where individuals need not remain identifiable

description.en: Go through the processing map and judge, per data action, whether its purpose can be met without identifying the individual, without records being linkable to each other, or without the processing being observable to other parties. Record the judgement and the reason on each action, including the actions judged to need full identification.

title.en: Generalise or suppress the attributes that still identify an individual

description.en: Work through the actions marked as not needing an identifiable individual and change the data itself: coarsen dates and locations, band small counts, drop the direct identifiers, and hold back the rare combinations only a handful of records share. Stripping name and account number rarely finishes the job — a postcode, a birth date and a job title together will name someone in a small population, so the question is whether any record still stands alone after the transformation, not whether the obvious fields are gone. Run the transformation where the data enters the non-identifying use rather than as a later pass over a copy, or the identifiable original keeps feeding whatever reads it.

evidenceHint.en: The transformation applied to each treated data set, naming the fields dropped, the values coarsened or banded and the records held back, with a before-and-after extract from one of them.

title.en: Review the identification retained against current purposes

description.en: For each data action, confirm the identification it still carries is required by the purpose it serves today rather than by a purpose it once served. List the actions where identification could now be reduced and name the owner of each reduction.

evidenceHint.en: Review list showing each data action, the identification retained, the purpose relied on, and whether a reduction was raised.

description.en: Implements CT.DP-P3: Data are processed to limit the formulation of inferences about individuals' behavior or activities (e.g., data processing is decentralized, distributed architectures).

title.en: List the deductions about behaviour and activity that must stay out of reach

description.en: A limit on inference is unenforceable until someone writes down which conclusions are off-limits: that a person was home on a Tuesday afternoon, that a household's occupancy changed, that somebody in a group is likely unwell. Work from the purpose each analysis actually serves, name the conclusions that reach past it, and separate those barred outright from those permitted only at group level above a stated size. Without that list every design argument collapses into whether the data is anonymous, which is a different question — an anonymous feed can still say what a household does each morning.

evidenceHint.en: Signed-off schedule of off-limits conclusions per analysis, marking which are barred outright and which are allowed only above a stated group size.

title.en: Reshape each analytic output so the barred conclusions cannot be drawn

description.en: De-identifying the inputs does not stop a result from announcing when a household wakes up, so the limit has to sit on what an analysis emits and not only on the records behind it. For each analysis pick whatever combination keeps a barred conclusion from following — computing where the data already sits and returning only totals, widening time and location bands, suppressing any cell below the agreed group size, or dropping a derived field nobody has a use for — and write the chosen setting beside the analysis it governs. Leave the reasoning attached, because a suppression threshold later relaxed for query performance will otherwise pass as routine tuning.

evidenceHint.en: Per-analysis configuration list naming the technique applied, the aggregation floor or band width in force, and the owner who set it.

title.en: Attempt each forbidden deduction against the outputs the system releases

description.en: Hand the released outputs to people who did not build the pipeline, together with whatever can be obtained publicly about the same population, and ask them to state what they can work out about one individual and about a small group. A deduction that fails only because this period's sample happened to be thin is not a control, so record against each attempt whether the design blocked it or the data did. Where an attempt succeeds, log the finding against the analysis that emitted the output rather than the store it drew from, because that is where the remedy has to go.

evidenceHint.en: Dated inference-attempt report listing each conclusion tried, the material used, the result, and whether design or sample size stopped it.

description.en: Implements CT.DP-P4: System or device configurations permit selective collection or disclosure of data elements.

title.en: Set the minimum selectivity a system must offer over what it gathers and sends

description.en: Before any product is examined, state the finest split the organisation expects to be able to make: which elements must be switchable on their own, which may be handled together as a group, and which are never optional. Without that standard the record of what each product allows has nothing to be judged against, and an all-or-nothing device passes simply because its single switch was written down. Name who may accept a product that cannot make the required split, and what they must put in writing when they do.

evidenceHint.en: Written standard listing the elements that must be individually controllable, those that may be grouped, the acceptance route for a product unable to meet it, and the named arbiter.

title.en: Record the collection and disclosure choices each system offers

description.en: For each system or device that allows a choice of which data elements are collected or released, record the setting in force, who set it and when it was last changed. Where a system offers no such choice, record that and name the owner who accepted collecting or releasing everything.

title.en: Re-check what each rebuilt or upgraded system now collects and releases

description.en: A selective setting is not done once: a re-image, a fleet re-provision or a vendor upgrade restores the supplier's default, and that default is almost always to gather and send everything on offer. For every system rebuilt, re-provisioned or upgraded since the last pass, read the setting back off the system itself rather than from the note made when it was first applied, and look for choices a newer release has added that nobody has taken up. Treat a reverted setting as a finding with a date attached, because how long it stood is the measure of what was gathered or released in the meantime.

evidenceHint.en: Per-system list of every rebuild, re-provision and version change in the period, the value read back from the live machine, the value expected, the date each divergence began, and any newly available choice left unused.

templates.title: Attribute references in place of values

description.en: Implements CT.DP-P5: Attribute references are substituted for attribute values.

title.en: Fix the properties a reference must have before it replaces a value

description.en: Decide ahead of any build whether a reference may be computed from the value it displaces, how much residual meaning it may carry, and which form a given case calls for: an opaque token that resolves only through a held mapping, or a derived assertion such as a band or a yes-or-no claim that resolves back to nothing. A reference calculated from its own value, a hash of an email address or a shortened account number, is not a substitution at all, because anyone with a list of plausible values recomputes it and reads the field. Written as conditions a proposed design is tested against, these properties stop each team settling the question privately and give a later check something it can fail.

evidenceHint.en: Agreed criteria for a valid substitution covering permitted derivation, residual meaning and the form required per case, with the reasoning and the approver for each condition.

title.en: Record where a reference stands in place of an attribute value

description.en: List the places where a stand-in is held instead of the value it represents, what each stands for, where the mapping back to the value lives, and who is able to resolve it. Record the places where the value itself is still held although a stand-in would serve.

title.en: Sweep the downstream stores for values a reference was meant to replace

description.en: A substitution holds only at the point it was applied, and the displaced value returns downstream by routes nobody rebuilt: an extract taken before the change, a support tool that writes the field into its diagnostics, a warehouse column still loaded from an older feed, a row carrying the reference and the original side by side. Work outward through the copies rather than re-reading the system where the reference is issued, because that system is the one place the substitution is already known to hold. For each original value found, settle whether it predates the substitution or a newer path reintroduced it, since only the second means the design is being bypassed and the store will fill again after a clean-up.

evidenceHint.en: Dated results listing every copy, extract, log sink and report examined, each original attribute still found in one, and whether an old load or a new integration put it there.

templates.title: Transparency policies and procedures
templates.description: Implements CM.PO-P1: Transparency policies, processes, and procedures for communicating data processing purposes, practices, associated privacy risks, and options for enabling individuals' data processing preferences and requests are established and in place.

title.en: Define what the organisation will tell individuals about its data processing

description.en: State which purposes, practices, privacy risks and available options must be communicated, and on what occasions a communication becomes owed — at collection, at a change, on request, after an event. Attach the transparency policy; it is the standard a later sample check measures issued communications against.

title.en: Trigger the transparency step from the approval of a processing change

description.en: Tie the transparency step to the approval that lets processing change — a new purpose, a new recipient, a shortened retention — so it opens before the change reaches individuals rather than when somebody remembers the policy exists. Fix how long a communication may lag the change it describes, name who hears about it when that period is running out, and have the functions granting those approvals acknowledge the step binds them. A procedure driven instead from the communications side always describes last quarter's processing, and the gap surfaces only when an individual compares what they were told against what is actually done.

evidenceHint.en: The issued procedure naming which approval opens the step, the period allowed before individuals hear of the change, and one recent change walked through it.

title.en: Check a sample of issued communications against the transparency policy

description.en: Take communications actually issued since the last check and confirm each covered what the policy requires for its occasion. Record every omission, the role that approved the communication, and whether the gap lies in the communication or in the policy.

evidenceHint.en: Sample check naming the communications reviewed, the policy points each was measured against, and every omission found with its cause.

templates.title: Roles for communicating data processing
templates.description: Implements CM.PO-P2: Roles and responsibilities (e.g., public relations) for communicating data processing purposes, practices, and associated privacy risks are established.

title.en: Assign the roles that draft, approve and issue privacy communications

description.en: Name the role that drafts a privacy communication, the role that approves its content, and the role that speaks when a privacy matter reaches the public, and record where the boundary between them sits and who acts when one is unavailable. Record the assignment against the named roles rather than against individuals who may move.

title.en: Refresh the holder and stand-in for every communication role each period

description.en: An assignment names roles, but a role with no occupant behind it cannot approve or speak, so each period carry every named communication role through to a person today and an identified cover, and record the reassignments made since the last pass. Publish it where anyone fielding a question about the organisation's data processing can see who holds the role now, instead of routing it to whoever answered last time. Keep the dated history alongside the current state: a communication issued three months ago has to be attributable to whoever held the approval then, not to whoever holds it today.

evidenceHint.en: The standing list of who holds each communication role and who covers for them, showing where it is published and the dated reassignments made since the previous update.

title.en: Trace each privacy communication back to the person who approved it

description.en: Take the privacy communications and public statements made since the last review and name, for each, who drafted it, who signed it off and who delivered it, then set that against the roles the assignment gives those jobs to; whether the content itself was adequate is a separate check. The failures worth finding are the item that went out with no sign-off at all, and the one approved by whichever senior person happened to be reachable — both mean the organisation is running on something other than the assignment it wrote down. Where a named holder repeatedly did not perform their part, decide whether the assignment moves or the behaviour does, and record which was chosen.

evidenceHint.en: Attribution table covering the period's communications with drafter, approver and speaker set against the assigned roles, listing every unapproved or misrouted item and the decision taken on it.

templates.title: Mechanisms for communicating data processing
templates.description: Implements CM.AW-P1: Mechanisms (e.g., notices, internal or public reports) for communicating data processing purposes, practices, associated privacy risks, and options for enabling individuals' preferences and requests are established and in place.

title.en: Record how each required communication reaches individuals

description.en: For every item the transparency policy requires be communicated, record the means by which it currently reaches individuals or the public, where it sits today, and when it was last changed. Where an item is required but reaches nobody, record that as an open row with an owner.

title.en: Build the notice and the report that each named channel will carry

description.en: Turn each entry on the channel list into an artefact that actually exists: the notice a person meets at the point of collection, the internal report that reaches management, the public report if one has been promised. Each has to carry the purposes, the practices and the privacy risks in language its audience can act on, and — the part most often left out — what the individual may ask for and where to ask for it. A notice that explains the processing but names no route for a preference or a request is only half a mechanism, and the symptom is requests arriving at whatever address people can find. Where the channel list showed a communication that is owed but has no artefact behind it, this is where that gap closes.

evidenceHint.en: The artefacts as issued — the notice as an individual sees it and the report as it was circulated — each carrying a version marker, an issue date, and the channel from the scoping list it was placed in.

title.en: Send out each periodic report and reissue the notice when processing changes

description.en: A mechanism counts as in place only while it is being worked: the periodic report has to go out on the cadence it claims, and the notice has to be replaced once the processing it describes has moved on. The failure here is quiet — a new purpose, a new recipient or a longer retention goes live while the published notice still describes last year's arrangement, leaving the organisation on record saying something that is no longer true. Treat any change that would alter a sentence of the notice as the trigger to reissue, rather than waiting for an annual refresh. Keep the superseded version instead of overwriting it, because a later question about what someone was told will be about the wording live on the day they were told it.

evidenceHint.en: Issue log for the period: each report despatched with its date and who received it, each notice version superseded, and the processing change that forced the replacement.

templates.title: Mechanisms for obtaining individual feedback
templates.description: Implements CM.AW-P2: Mechanisms for obtaining feedback from individuals (e.g., surveys or focus groups) about data processing and associated privacy risks are established and in place.

title.en: Fit feedback instruments to the populations whose data is processed

description.en: Take the categories of individuals the processing touches and decide, for each, the means by which the organisation will ask them what they make of it — a questionnaire, a moderated session, a standing panel, an open form — then stand that means up so it is capable of receiving an answer today rather than in principle. One instrument rarely covers everyone: people who never sign in cannot see an in-product prompt, former customers no longer receive the mailing, and a group whose data arrived through an employer, a school or a broker has no direct line at all. Give each instrument a named owner and a destination the responses actually land in, because a route nobody empties has not been established, only announced.

evidenceHint.en: The instruments as they currently stand — question wording, session plan, form — listed against the category of individuals each is meant to reach and the owner who empties it.

title.en: Solicit individuals' views on the processing and record what came back

description.en: Ask individuals directly what they make of the processing and the risks it carries, by whatever means suits the population, and record the responses received and what was done with them. This is the organisation going to individuals; complaints arriving unprompted are handled through the monitoring intake instead.

evidenceHint.en: Record of the solicitation showing who was asked, when, what came back, and the changes considered or made as a result.

title.en: Judge each feedback route by who actually answered it

description.en: Set the responses arriving since the last check against the categories of individuals the processing covers, and note for each route how many people it was capable of reaching as well as how many replied. A route that returns nothing is ambiguous — it can mean contentment, or that it reached no one — so state which of the two the evidence supports instead of letting an empty inbox pass as approval. Where a category has stayed silent across two checks running, name the instrument that will be changed for it and the person changing it.

evidenceHint.en: Reach and response counts per category of individuals for the period, with a stated reason for every silent category and the instrument change agreed against it.

templates.title: In-product data processing visibility
templates.description: Implements CM.AW-P3: System/product/service design enables data processing visibility.

title.en: Record what each system shows an individual about the processing of their data

description.en: For every system with which individuals interact directly, record what they can see about what is being done with their data and what options they can exercise there. Where a system shows nothing, record that and name the owner of the decision to leave it so.

title.en: Drive the product as an individual and compare its view to what ran

description.en: An in-product view built from a hand-written summary drifts the moment a feature starts reading a new element, and nobody notices because the screen still renders. Sign in to a genuine account that has real activity behind it, visit every place the product claims to tell the person what is happening to their data, and set the elements, purposes and recipients named on screen against those the system actually touched for that account. Anything the processing did that no screen accounts for is the finding, not the pass.

evidenceHint.en: Dated walkthrough per system naming the test account, the screens visited, and every element, purpose or recipient the processing touched that the interface never named.

title.en: Challenge designs that leave a data action invisible inside the product

description.en: Visibility is decided at design time, so the gap appears in a specification rather than in a test run: a feature is built with no screen, indicator or setting through which the person would ever learn it ran. Take the data actions added or altered since the last cycle and, for each one with nowhere in the interface an individual could see it, force a ruling — the design gains a surface, or a named owner accepts the blind spot and states why. A published notice is not an answer here, because what is under examination is what the product itself reveals to the person using it.

evidenceHint.en: Design review minutes listing each data action added or altered in the period, whether the interface exposes it, and the owner and reasoning behind every accepted blind spot.
